synth.canonicalReviewModel: CANONICAL_RULE: the canon already DEFINES the requirement but not the contract. Owner lock L-017 / item 16 of 21 (2026-09-02): 1-5 stars + OPTIONAL short text comment after a completed Dogovor, no multi-axis form; public profile may show average, count, completed count and review content [CR-01, M18]. Display rules D-0128..D-0131: individual rows with the real stars + real comment when present, reviewer public avatar/name, tap to reviewer profile, relative age from the immutable review timestamp, star-only entries stay star-only; D-0128 literally names the REQUESTER profile (corrected in M18) [CR-09]. Product direction 'comment: YES' was approved 2026-09-24 and restated 2026-10-01, always conditional on a separate server/schema/privacy/moderation package and the owner's exact word; the EX-04 application receipt records D12 as NOT approved [CR-02, CR-03, C-31]. FACT_LIVE_DEV (ledger 219, certificate 58447d77): ONE table private.agreement_reviews (id, agreement_id, reviewer_account_id, target_account_id, rating 1..5, tags text[] from a 6-code catalog max 3, client_request_id, input_hash, created_at), 7 rows, NO text column anywhere (information_schema scan), immutable by trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE for every role, RLS enabled+forced, 0 policies, ACL postgres only, reachable only via rpc_submit_agreement_review(uuid,uuid,jsonb,jsonb,uuid), rpc_get_my_agreement_review(uuid), rpc_get_account_reputation(uuid); public aggregate = account-level count + round(avg,2) inside rpc_get_public_profile; no function lists another person's individual review [R01-R05, R11-R13, E01-E04]. 32 live function bodies equal the repository (pins in E18). OPEN in canon and NOT to be invented: review deadline, edit, publication timing / blind reveal, account-score vs role views (F144), every numeric limit, retention period, moderation operator and effect [CR-07, M21, DEC-1..DEC-6]. Tags are 'superseded' in final canon but live in source and DEV (4 of 7 reviews) - leave untouched [DN-01].
synth.whoMayWrite: CANONICAL_RULE + FACT_LIVE_DEV: only a participant of an Agreement may review the counterpart; Agreement.status AND agreement_execution.state must both be COMPLETED; own review must not exist; reviewer must not be closure-restricted (PostgREST pre-request guard ACCOUNT_CLOSING plus BEFORE INSERT trigger on the reviewer) [R07, R08, E05, E14]. PROPOSAL: the comment adds NO new eligibility - it rides on exactly the same gate as the stars (a stricter gate would be invented policy). Skeptic correction R07: COMPLETED is also reached by the 48h requester auto-completion (rpc_tick_auto_completion, service-only) and by requester confirmation after a reported problem; there is no review deadline, so a comment becomes possible after both paths; default = allowed (same as stars), flagged for owner confirmation [DN-04, D-DEC-11]. Tested canon behaviour kept: the counterpart may still review a closure-restricted target (account_closure_proof.mjs:76-81) and a block does not remove the review entitlement [CZ-8, R09]. Helpers never review (lead only, spec 112) [CR-06].
synth.oneReviewRule: CANONICAL_RULE: unique(agreement_id, reviewer_account_id) = at most one review per participant per Agreement, so at most two per Agreement (one per side); retry of the same direction is idempotent (reviewer, client_request_id) and never creates a second review [R03, R10, CR-06]. The review is an immutable single command (trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE, client copy 'Uspesna ocena se ne menja'). PROPOSAL consistent with canon: the comment travels ATOMICALLY in the same command as the stars; there is no separate comment step. Consequences to state to the owner: (1) a star-only review (any installed APK, or a person who skips the text) can NEVER gain a comment later, because that would be an edit, which canon does not define [R28, DEC-5, C-11]; (2) the 7 existing DEV reviews stay comment-less forever; (3) ratingDue / Home 'Cekaju te' predicates stay unchanged because they are defined by review-row existence, so a comment does not alter them [E21, M31]; (4) the review row and its input_hash formula stay byte-identical, the comment lives in its own row keyed 1:1 by review_id (PK), so 'one review per side' remains the single rule and 'at most one comment per review' follows from the PK.
synth.textRulesProposal: PROPOSAL - canon names NO number or validation rule for 'short' (L-017 says only 'short'/'bounded input') [DN-02, M27, C-32]; every item below needs the owner's word before application. (a) Optional: no preselected text, no obligation, empty/whitespace-only means NO comment (omitted, never stored as an empty row) [CR-05]. (b) Length: 1..500 characters counted as code points after btrim (char_length), plus octet_length <= 2000; 500 matches the existing close-search/QA bound and stays below 1000 (application message), 2000 (chat, safety narrative) [DN-02, M11]. (c) Strictness: server REJECTS rather than silently normalises (text must equal btrim(text), no NUL, no control characters except LF; reject CR/TAB, bidi controls U+200E/U+200F/U+202A-202E/U+2066-2069, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2028/2029; allow U+200D and U+FE0F so emoji sequences work) because [[:cntrl:]] alone misses U+202E and U+200B [M10] and a server that normalises would break the client's readback-equality check and make a successful save look like REVIEW_INVALID_RECEIPT [C-10]. Client sends trimmed NFC text; count unit and rule written once into the server contract and ONE shared client helper (today the helper is duplicated in 5 services) [M11, C-10]. (d) Type strictness: p_comment is jsonb and must be JSON null or a JSON string (as p_rating is a strict JSON number). (e) Deterministic contact floor, NO AI and NO paid call: reuse private.ru4b_public_floor_reason(text) (IMMUTABLE, uncertified, not in the 88) to reject e-mail, links, @handles and phone numbers with ONE plain-Serbian code REVIEW_COMMENT_CONTACT_NOT_PUBLIC; measured limits: it flags '064 123 4567' and e-mails but MISSES spelled-out numbers and obfuscated addresses, so it is a floor, not a guarantee; the Q&A AI policy gate is NOT reused [M09, C-24 corrected, DN-12]. (f) Errors: validation raises 22023 with names REVIEW_COMMENT_INVALID / REVIEW_COMMENT_TOO_LONG / REVIEW_COMMENT_CONTACT_NOT_PUBLIC; no 40001 anywhere; any deterministic conflict that appears must use PT409 [CE-5]. Every new name needs an entry in the client errors map or it degrades to the generic unknown-outcome text [C-09]. The legacy 5-argument path must never raise a new name [R18 addition]. (g) Idempotency: star row input_hash formula unchanged ({agreementId,target,rating,tags}); the comment is bound by comment_sha256 stored in the comment row; same request id + different comment (or comment added to a stored star-only review) = REQUEST_ID_REUSED. This keeps the 7 stored hashes, old-APK lost-ack replays and replays through either function byte-compatible, and keeps the free-text fingerprint inside the erasable row [R10, A-hash, CZ-5].
synth.visibility: CANONICAL_RULE: public profile directly beneath the authoritative average/count shows individual eligible rows with real stars + real comment, reviewer avatar/name from the authorised public projection (no phone/email/address), tap on avatar/name opens that reviewer's profile with safe failure, relative age from the immutable review timestamp, private job and address never on the card; list and aggregate share one eligibility/moderation truth (D-0128..D-0131, J23) [CR-09]. Today NO reader exists: installed clients show only count + average, the reviewed person sees only the aggregate and a generic notification, tags and ratings are visible only in the reviewer's own receipt [R11, R13, C-15]. PROPOSAL: (1) the author sees the own comment in the own receipt (new context reader, see schemaOutline); (2) a NEW separate paged reader rpc_list_review_comments_v1 keyed by PROFILE id, NOT folded into rpc_get_public_profile (that RPC is called per card by candidate/Discovery readers) [R13, C-16, A-7]; (3) it copies the rpc_get_public_profile gate stack exactly: authenticated only, ACTIVE profile, closure-restricted caller/target -> null, safety_pair_blocked -> null, accounts_same_world (TEST world) - NOT the rpc_get_account_reputation stack, which has no world check [R25, A7, DN-14 corrected]; (4) also hide a row whose AUTHOR is closure-restricted (existing readers fence only viewer and subject) [A-author-fence]; (5) read-time block rule: a comment whose author/subject pair is currently blocked either way is not listed, without any write-time refusal because a refusal would reveal the block to the blocked person; stars still count [A-block, DN-14]; (6) role: account-level list (reputation is one account score, F144/DN-21); the author's displayed profile is derived from the Agreement role of the reviewer (requester or worker profile) - the exact projection fields must be read from the live rpc_get_public_profile body while generating the candidate (not verified here); (7) keyset paging on (created_at desc, review_id), page limit default 20, max 50, partial index on the comment table; 8 s authenticated statement_timeout [R25]; (8) PROPOSAL needing owner word: the reader lists ONLY reviews that carry a visible comment; legacy and future star-only reviews stay aggregate-only. This avoids retroactively making the 7 existing star-only reviews individually attributable public data that their authors gave under the aggregate-only table contract [live addition retroactive-disclosure, R11]; it deviates from D-0128/F139 literal 'every eligible row' and must be disclosed and confirmed. DECISION_NEEDED: Requester-profile-only (D-0128 literal) vs both profiles; where the reviewed person reads comments about themselves (own public profile has no route today) [C-20, DN-06, DN-07].
synth.publicProfileAndReputation: FACT_LIVE_DEV: reputation = one account-level count + average over agreement_reviews.target_account_id, both roles pooled, no cache, no role split; rpc_get_public_profile trust block = {ratingAverage, reviewCount, completedCount, identityVerified:false, ratingAvailable, reviewsAvailable:true (hard-coded), identityVerificationAvailable:false}; app_profiles.rating_requester/rating_worker are a dead cache (0 of 10) so reviews do not feed matching [R12-R14]. PROPOSAL (leave all of this byte-identical): rpc_get_account_reputation (4166221185), rpc_get_public_profile (9ecc0b69), account_reputation (f03e558f) are NOT edited; reviewCount keeps meaning 'number of star ratings' and must never become a comment count, otherwise decoders that require count/average/ratingAvailable consistency throw PUBLIC_PROFILE_RATING_INVALID in installed APKs [C-05]. A comment never feeds any score or ranking (no sentiment, no AI). Comments appear only through the separate reader (section visibility), loaded on demand when the person opens the comments section of the profile sheet, with its own loading/empty/error+retry states, so the Discovery/candidate cards (EX-03 area, up to 100 profiles per slice) pay nothing [C-16]. Vocabulary: the UI today calls the star count 'recenzija' on the public sheet/candidate cards and 'ocena' on the own profile; PROPOSAL: counts stay 'ocena' (they count stars) and the written part is 'komentar' [C-17]. No hidden-star penalty: moderating a comment never changes stars, count or average (D-0069, DN-09).
synth.reportModerationPath: FACT_LIVE_DEV / GAP: there is NO review-specific report, hide, remove or restore path. Existing primitives: rpc_submit_safety_report (account-keyed, categories HARASSMENT/FRAUD/UNSAFE_WORK/DISCRIMINATION/OTHER, reason <=200, narrative <=2000, agreement or need context, no quota by AF-D17, works between blocked pairs, md5 9249705c) and support topic CONTENT_NOTICE ('Prijava sadrzaja ili recenzije', quota 5 cases/24h, 60 s cooldown); support reference kinds are only TASK, AGREEMENT, AGREEMENT_MESSAGE, GROUP_MESSAGE, TASK_REVIEW (= the AI publication draft review, NOT the Agreement review) and SAFETY_REPORT; support_decisions_v5 is hard-CHECKed to effect = 'NONE'; support_operator_grants_v5 has 0 active rows; 0 reports, 0 blocks, 0 cases on DEV, never exercised [M01-M06, M17, M24, E12]. CANONICAL_RULE: a report is NOT an instant removal; a real eligibility change must move feed and aggregate together; AI may only triage, human decides; a report button pointing at an unattended table is not finished operations (APL-06); AF-D18: support decisions may not change a review and a new public policy exception is a separate owner decision [CR-11, M05, M19]. PROPOSAL, minimal and old-client-safe: (1) REPORT = existing channels only, NO new vocabulary: a 'Prijavi' entry on a listed comment opens the existing SafetyScreen (target = the author's account, agreementId context for the reviewed person; third parties report the account under the ACTIVE-profile fallback) or the existing CONTENT_NOTICE case. Reason: a new support reference kind or topic or safety category is NOT old-client-safe (strict whitelisting decoders return null for the whole inbox page/case) AND edits five certified functions (support_reference_v5, rpc_support_find_context_v5, rpc_support_submit_v5, closure_support_source_fence_v5, closure_erasure_exceptions_v5) [C-23 corrected, A4]. Cost: no structured pointer, the operator finds the comment by agreement id + author. (2) MODERATION ACTION, only if the owner approves an effect: hide the COMMENT TEXT only (hidden_at + reason code on the comment row), stars, count, average and ratingDue untouched; service_role-only audited function rpc_moderate_review_comment_service_v1(action HIDE|RESTORE, reason code ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$, request id) writing marketplace_audit_log (open vocabulary, entity AGREEMENT, detail ids + reason code only); no auto-hide, no AI, no SLA text, no author notification in V1 (a new event type would change the closed user_activity_events CHECK); the owner as the single private-test operator; production operator, response time and appeal are explicit owner inputs (LEG-14 not started) and remain a release gate [DN-09, DN-10, E13]. This is a NEW public-policy exception under AF-D18, so it needs the owner's explicit word. All moderation proof is disposable-chain only (no operator grant, 0 cases on DEV) [A8, M17].
synth.abuseAndSpamControl: FACT_LIVE_DEV: no rate-limit, quota, profanity, PII or abuse machinery exists for reviews, reports, blocks or chat; the only volume bounds are unique(agreement_review per side) + the completion gate; DEV (7 reviews, 2 accounts) proves nothing about farming; whether Agreement creation between the same two accounts is bounded was NOT verified [E13, M12 corrected, A9 UNVERIFIABLE]. PROPOSAL, deterministic only, no AI and no paid service: (1) structural bound = one comment per review, <=2 per Agreement, only after real completion; (2) validation of the textRulesProposal (length, control/format characters, strictness, contact floor) enforced in the server function AND by CHECK on the table; (3) NO new per-account/per-day cap (a number would be invented policy; precedent for caps exists only for support 5/24h and Q&A 10/24h); offered as an optional owner choice; (4) the legacy 5-argument path is untouched (cannot carry text); (5) idempotent command with advisory locks (command + (agreement,reviewer)), concurrency proof must show exactly one row; (6) report-bombing: AF-D17 deliberately exempts safety reports from quotas while LEG-07 promises protection from report abuse; PROPOSAL: do not change AF-D17 in this package, route comment reports through the throttled CONTENT_NOTICE topic where possible, record as owner call [M28]; (7) block interplay: text by a blocked author is silently hidden at read time, not refused [A-block]; (8) residual risk stated honestly: street addresses, names and third-party personal data in free text cannot be detected deterministically (LEG-09 P-19/G-10) [DEC-4, E-privacy]; store UGC rules (Apple 1.2, Google UGC: acceptance of terms, report/block, published contact, timely action) stay explicit RELEASE gates, not DEV blockers [FS-04, DN-19].
synth.privacyClassification: PROPOSAL (legal/privacy classification is an owner/legal decision; nothing here is legal certification): the comment is user-authored free text = ordinary personal content of the AUTHOR that is also personal data ABOUT the reviewed person, may contain third-party and special-category data that cannot be technically excluded, and is visible to signed-in same-world users via the reader. Classify under the EXISTING retention class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS (required+active); do NOT add a 16th class: a 16th required class reopens any published schedule and breaks the closure Edge worker (hard-coded retainedDatasets.length !== 15) and the client label map [RT-4 verified, live addition class coupling]. Rules the package must enforce and prove: never in push, notification payload, inbox, audit detail, RAISE messages, logs or AI context (AI/provider flows never receive reviews, LEG-04:109); no new processor (stored only in Supabase; no Edge function reads agreement_reviews); event REVIEW_RECEIVED keeps payload '{}' and the fixed copy [C-19, RT-5, E19]. Current docs ASSERT THE OPPOSITE and must be updated in the same package: LEG-02 s23, LEG-04 s3.2/s11/s14/s16, LEG-05 s11, LEG-07 s11, LEG-08 s5/s6, LEG-09 P-19/G-10, LEG-10 row 9 + decision 8, DATA_DECLARATIONS_DRAFT GS-23, REVIEW_NOTES_DRAFT:145, STORE_LISTING_DRAFTS:68, AF22_CLOSURE_INVENTORY_144.json ('Bounded tags, no free text'), EXPORT_PROJECTION.md (stale 37 datasets / V5_1), in-app closure copy ClosurePresentation.tsx:137-139 [R21, DEC-6, E20]. DPIA need remains [[PROVERITI]]; lawful basis and retention are owner/legal inputs.
synth.exportCoverage: FACT_LIVE_DEV: export = 52 datasets (catalog md5 7fc01c56, snapshot b198bff5, projection version OWN_ACCOUNT_V5_9); the only review dataset is ownAgreementReviews (fields agreementId, createdAt, id, rating, tags; filter reviewer_account_id = requester AND participant), i.e. only reviews the person WROTE; reviews written ABOUT the person are not exported [EX-1, EX-2, E10]. Export functions are NOT among the 88 certified functions, so export edits do not move the certificate, but they change data_export_projection_sha_v5() (md5 chain of 6 functions) which a published policy's export_delivery.projectionSha256 must equal; data_export_policy_binding() hard-codes the projection version literal and the dataset count 52 [EX-3, EX-4]. On DEV the binding is NULL (0 retention policy sets, 0 legal documents, one request stuck in REQUESTED, 0 artifacts), so export is EXPORT_POLICY_NOT_READY and cannot be demonstrated on real DEV data at all [EX-5, E06]. PROPOSAL: add the author's OWN comment as a field of the existing ownAgreementReviews dataset (comment, plus hidden state is NOT exported as moderation data) so the count stays 52; edit catalog + snapshot + the projection-version literal (V5_9 -> V5_10, in snapshot and policy binding); published policy must target the new projectionSha256 later; do NOT export comments received about a person (EX-6): exporting received text would put a copy of the author's words into the target's artifact that the author's closure cannot erase (artifacts are scoped by t.account_id = owner) [live addition]; copies inside the author's own export artifacts are already erased by the existing closure DELETE of data_export_artifacts [EX-7]. Proof (disposable chain only, with a published test policy): own comment present, peer comment absent, dataset count 52, version/sha as designed, canary absent from snapshot_text after closure. Update the stale 37-dataset assertion note in v5_owned_export_proof (line 87) when touching that proof.
synth.closureAndDeletion: FACT_LIVE_DEV: private.agreement_reviews is NOT in closure_redaction_relations_v5 (75 relations), has no scope/patch branch, and guard_review_immutable raises unconditionally (no closure carve-out); so today closure retains the whole review row (ids, rating, tags) as pseudonymous minimum and erases nothing relational; 0 closures ever executed on DEV, so no proof exists for reviews at closure [CL-2, E08, E11, CZ-2, CZ-4]. CANONICAL_RULE: AF-D22 - at closure delete or anonymise ordinary personal content, no invented exception durations; owner 2026-09-19 - no arbitrary human-entered free text survives a closure without a separate future owner decision; SHARED_AUTHORED precedent - only the closing author's own text is erased, the counterpart's content stays (messages 'Sadrzaj uklonjen pri zatvaranju naloga.', LEG-08 s6) [CL-4, CZ-3, CR-13]. PROPOSAL (separate comment table, see schemaOutline): (1) AUTHOR closes: the comment row is DELETEd by the existing closure executor (new DELETE branch mirroring the private.data_export_artifacts branch of closure_redaction_patch_v5, scope t.author_account_id=$1); the star row stays untouched (pseudonymous minimum), aggregate and ratingDue unchanged; the delete is allowed only through closure_redaction_allowed_v5 (certificate row + EXECUTING closure with adapter OWNER_AF_D22_EVENT_ERASURE_V1) in the new trigger function, so ordinary UPDATE/DELETE keep failing. (2) Edited certified functions (all inside the 88): closure_redaction_relations_v5 (append at the END: 75 -> 76 steps, worker/client accept 1..1000), closure_redaction_scope_v5, closure_redaction_patch_v5; append the table to the AGREEMENT_REVIEWS row of closure_dataset_catalog_v5 (a data update, digest-invisible) [E09, CZ-6]. DO NOT edit guard_review_immutable, closure_guard_owned_write, closure_account_restricted, closure_assert_open, closure_account_key (the last three are md5-pinned inside retention_ai_source_ready) [live addition]. (3) Protected Agreement: PROPOSAL = like chat messages, the comment is erased regardless of Agreement protection; the account-level SCOPED_EVIDENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED exception still surfaces; retention-as-evidence would be a different precedent (responses/versions are skipped) and is an owner call [E09 corrected]. (4) TARGET closes: PROPOSAL default = comment is hidden by the reader gates (target restricted) and NOT erased (follows author-scope precedent and LEG-08 s6); the alternative 'erase on either side' (matches the AF22 inventory ownerScope 'reviewer OR target') is a one-clause scope change plus its own proof; LEG-10 decision 8 is unresolved, DECISION_NEEDED [DEC-2, CL-2]. (5) The hidden/moderation state does not survive as free text because the whole row is deleted. (6) A new table with client-reachable ACL would NOT be closure-fenced: keep it in schema private, ACL postgres only [CZ-9].
synth.retention: GAP: NO canonical retention period exists for ratings, tags or comments (private.retention_policy_sets = 0, rules = 0; LEG-10 row 9 'dok nalog postoji' and decision 8 are unapproved technical proposals; table comment: 'Retention execution requires separately approved binding') [RT-1, RT-3, E06]. AF-D22 (owner) gives only a shape: no automatic 30-day deletion, history stays while the account exists, closure deletes/anonymises personal content, no invented durations; it does not literally name ratings/comments (applied by analogy) [RT-2]; D-0141 item 5 and AGENTS 3.4.5 forbid inventing a duration. PROPOSAL: the package states NO number; comment retention = 'while the author's account exists, deleted at the author's closure, hidden comments retained (not purged) for the same unknown period, no scheduler'; AGREEMENT_REVIEWS stays the one class; the retention period for the pseudonymous review minimum and for the other side's reviews remains an explicit owner/legal input (LEG-10 questions 5 and 8). Numbers that look like periods (export ceilings 2,592,000 s/900 s, review expiry 15 min, push/tick timers, LEG-10 technical proposals) are NOT retention and must not be copied [RT-3]. Backups, provider copies and device-local state have no defined retention; D12 adds no processor [RT-5]. If the client ever persists a draft it enters LEG-09 P-27 - PROPOSAL: memory-only draft (support-form precedent), never persisted [C-25 corrected].
synth.rlsAcl: FACT_LIVE_DEV baseline to reproduce for every new object: private.agreement_reviews has RLS enabled AND forced, 0 policies, relacl {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres}, no column ACLs, not in any publication; authenticated/anon/service_role have no USAGE on schema private and no table privilege; review RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=pg_catalog, EXECUTE only for postgres + authenticated [R05, R06, E01, E03]. pg_default_acl grants arwdDxtm/EXECUTE to anon, authenticated and service_role for NEW objects in schema public but there is NO default ACL for schema private [live addition default privileges]. PROPOSAL: (1) table private.agreement_review_comments_v1 in schema private (never another schema: both digests only look at public/private + storage.objects), owner postgres, ENABLE + FORCE RLS, 0 policies, REVOKE ALL from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role (explicit even though private has no default ACL), relacl exactly {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres}; relacl/RLS flags are hashed by the program digest so a wrong ACL moves the certificate. (2) Public functions are created in schema public, so REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC/anon/service_role explicitly and GRANT EXECUTE to authenticated only for rpc_submit_agreement_review_v2, rpc_get_my_agreement_review_v2, rpc_list_review_comments_v1; rpc_moderate_review_comment_service_v1 = service_role (+postgres) only, authenticated denied; all SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = pg_catalog, schema-qualified references. (3) A new RPC is automatically default-denied for a closure-restricted caller by rpc_closure_api_guard (path-based, no edit needed; md5 09d52bad stays) [E14]. (4) No RLS policy is needed (access only through definer functions); the existing restrictive policy v5_closed_account_visibility pattern only applies to public tables, so nothing client-reachable may live in public [CZ-9]. (5) Proof: has_table_privilege / has_function_privilege / has_schema_privilege matrix for anon, authenticated, service_role, postgres, plus the default-ACL diff.
synth.oldClients: FACT_SOURCE: every installed build (APK 93e48799/bf48a5db, baseline 11574c02, emulator builds; the not-yet-installed 9ef10b67) shares the same review call shape - exactly five named args p_agreement_id, p_target_account_id, p_rating, p_tags, p_client_request_id - unchanged since commit 04c0000a; decoders read named keys and ignore extra keys, but hard-pin tagCatalog.version PRE_V3_REVIEW_TAGS_V1, maxTags 3 and the exact six-tag list, require eligible/review coupling, and treat any error name missing from their errors map as a generic unknown outcome [R18, C-02, C-04, C-05, C-33, R18 addition]. R19/C-06 verified only PARTLY: exactly one overload exists live, but a PostgREST ambiguity (PGRST203) with an extra overload was NOT reproduced and the EX-04b drop-and-recreate precedent does not carry over (nothing called the old reader, while every installed APK calls this RPC) [R19 corrected]. PROPOSAL (lowest risk): leave ALL existing review functions BYTE-IDENTICAL (submit ff68b552, my_review 75a8b78e, reputation 41662211, public_profile 9ecc0b69, review_receipt 7058b3cc, guard_review_immutable f883b4ed, ex04c readers 5017f90f/1703b04e) and add NEW function names (precedent: rpc_send_agreement_message_v2 coexists live): rpc_submit_agreement_review_v2 and rpc_get_my_agreement_review_v2. Result: no overload ambiguity possible, no break of pinned surface evidence/regprocedure proofs (reviews_authority_proof.mjs:140, account_closure_proof 76-81, pkg023f surface evidence), ex04c pins stay valid, old clients keep the star-only path with no new error name, tagCatalog and all existing keys untouched, event/inbox/push copy untouched, REVIEW_RECEIVED payload stays '{}'. New client: presence of rpc_get_my_agreement_review_v2 IS the capability (PGRST202 on an older server -> old context + old submit, comment field hidden; all-or-none like ratingDue/ratings) [C-07]; the key p_comment is OMITTED when the person typed nothing; the field is shown only when v2 advertises commentPolicy. Old clients never display comments (no read path) and never get them in their own receipt; they still work for stars. Replay interoperability is proved: same client_request_id issued via the old function and replayed via v2 (and the reverse) returns idempotentReplay=true [A-hash]. Fallback if the owner insists on one function name: DROP the 5-arg and CREATE the 6-arg with default in ONE statement, but then PGRST resolution with the exact 5-key body must be proved through real PostgREST and the pinned proofs rewritten. Old-APK retirement of the legacy function is a later package (S04 rule: stop distributing first, drop last).
synth.editDelete: NOT DEFINED - owner decision. The canonical product defines the review as IMMUTABLE: trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE for every role, client copy 'Sacuvana ocena se ne menja', registry 'Immutable review command', LIVE D12 'ne uvoditi edit ocene zbog dizajna'; F144 keeps edit/deadline/publication OPEN with the instruction not to invent them; the runbook lists 'edit' only as a rule still to be completed [CR-08, R20, M21, DN-05]. Per the owner's own condition (edit/delete only if the canon already defines it) the recommendation is to ship V1 WITHOUT author edit and WITHOUT author delete: the comment is part of the same immutable review, the new comment trigger raises REVIEW_COMMENT_IMMUTABLE for every ordinary UPDATE/DELETE, and the ONLY removals are (a) author-closure erasure (AF-D22, certified path) and (b) a moderation HIDE if the owner approves it (a reversible flag on the comment, never an author action). If the owner later wants edit/delete he must state window, count, what stays visible and history; it becomes a follow-up package and moves the certificate again if it changes triggers or tables.

risks: RISK certificate: any new table/column/trigger moves 58447d77; applying without the atomic three-place re-bind makes closure_erasure_binding_v5() NULL and stops account closure for everyone (CLOSURE_POLICY_NOT_READY / CLOSURE_POLICY_CHANGED) [CE-2, RK-02 corrected, live addition].

RISK three pinned certified functions are edited (closure_redaction_relations/scope/patch); a wrong branch breaks closure for all accounts; closure has NEVER been executed on DEV (0 executions), so the only closure evidence is the disposable chain [E06, E11, E22].

RISK old clients: PGRST203 with an extra overload was NOT reproduced (UNVERIFIABLE) and the EX-04b precedent does not apply; mitigated by new function names and unchanged legacy RPCs, but the exact five-key call must still be proved through real PostgREST [R19 PARTLY, C-06].
RISK v2 is a full re-implementation of the submit logic: behavioural drift from the legacy function (hash, audit, event, error codes) is possible; mitigated only by the parity proof T3 [live design].

RISK idempotency: if the comment enters input_hash the 7 stored hashes and lost-ack replays break and a text fingerprint stays outside the erasable row; design keeps the star hash formula and stores comment_sha256 in the comment row [R10, CZ-5, A-hash].

RISK block hole: a blocked author can still publish text about the blocker (existing review entitlement is deliberate and tested); read-time hiding is a PROPOSAL; refusing at write time would leak the block [R09, A-block, M25].

RISK retaliation/publication timing: F144 forbids inventing a blind model; immediate publication with stars exposes the reviewed person to identify and answer the author; D-0129 identity disclosure is a locked owner decision that the owner should re-confirm for free text [RK-01, DN-03, DN-08].

RISK retroactive disclosure: making existing star-only reviews individually attributable would break the aggregate-only table contract; the PROPOSAL lists only commented reviews but deviates from D-0128/F139 literal [live addition, DN-06].

RISK world fence: rpc_get_account_reputation has no accounts_same_world check; a comment reader modelled on it would leak across the TEST world (owner accounts are in the TEST world, pkg029e); copy rpc_get_public_profile instead [R25, A7, CR-15].

RISK role mismatch: reviews are account-level while profiles are per role; the displayed author profile must be derived from the Agreement role; F144 account-vs-role display remains an explicit owner question [live addition, DN-21].

RISK abuse: no rate limit, no content filter beyond a deterministic floor that misses spelled-out numbers, obfuscated e-mails and bidi/zero-width characters unless added explicitly; collusion/farming through repeated small Agreements was NOT verified (UNVERIFIABLE) [M09, M10, A9].

RISK moderation is unexercised and unstaffed: 0 reports, 0 blocks, 0 cases, 0 operator grants on DEV; LEG-14 not started; support decisions are hard-limited to effect NONE; a hide action is a NEW public-policy exception (AF-D18); store UGC rules (Apple 1.2, Google UGC) become hard release gates [M17, M24, FS-04, DN-10].

RISK reporting: a new support reference kind/topic/safety category is NOT old-client-safe (strict decoders) and edits five certified functions; AF-D17 leaves safety reports unlimited (report-bombing) [C-23 corrected, M28].

RISK legal/documentation contradiction: nine drafts and the AF22 inventory currently state that no free-text review exists; CI also deep-equals table columns against the inventory (v5_account_erasure_proof.mjs, v5_account_erasure.test.mjs) so the package fails CI if they are not updated together [R21, E20, privacy addition].

RISK export: export cannot run on DEV (binding NULL, 0 policies, 0 legal documents); exporting received comments would copy the author's text into the target's artifact beyond the author's closure; the projection sha/version bump invalidates any future policy written against the old sha [EX-5, live addition, A3].
RISK retention: no approved period; LEG-10 decision 8 (other side's review) unresolved; a 16th retention class would break the closure Edge worker and client label map [RT-3, RT-4, live addition].

RISK proof-chain fidelity: the Voice B1 chain omits EX-04a-d (ledger 216-219) although ex04c rewrote the ratingDue readers; the disposable digest never equals the DEV digest; candidate headers can be stale (ex04c header still says NOT APPLIED; migration header 'NOT LIVE') so pin by live md5, not by file headers [E17 corrected, R16, R17, E20].

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-1: Approve the closure/privacy certificate re-bind (isolated recertification) as part of the atomic D12 apply, with a revert that REFUSES while any comment exists?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: AGENTS 3.1.4: any change that moves the certified digest needs an isolated recertification and the owner's explicit approval; D12 cannot be function-only (new table + 3 certified functions). Blocks the APPLICATION only, not writing the candidate. The approval block must name the re-bind (Voice B1 precedent).
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: one atomic apply including the three-place re-bind; separate table (not a column on the immutable star table); say explicitly that old APKs are unaffected because the legacy RPCs stay byte-identical; owner words 'PRIMENI D12 PISANI KOMENTAR' only after proofs and a fresh read-only preflight.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-2: Moderation effect and operator - may a moderator HIDE a comment (comment text only, stars and aggregate untouched), who operates it, and is there any author notification?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Canon requires a moderation truth consistent between feed and aggregate (W10, D-0128, F143) but AF-D18 says support decisions cannot change a review and any new public-policy exception needs its own explicit decision; support operator is a singleton PRIVATE_TEST account with no active grant; LEG-14 not started. The answer decides whether the comment table carries hidden_* columns and whether a moderation function exists, so it changes the schema and the reader.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: hide comment text only (reversible hidden_at + reason code), service_role-only audited function used by the owner in the private test, no auto-hide, no AI, no SLA text, no author notification in V1; production operator and response time stay explicit owner inputs and a release gate.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-3: Report pointer for a comment - existing channels only (safety report / CONTENT_NOTICE, no structured pointer) or a structured review reference?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: A structured reference needs a new support reference kind or a review_id on safety reports: it edits five certified support functions, moves the certificate a second time if added later, and breaks strict old-client support decoders (C-23 corrected). The existing channels need no certified change but give no exact pointer.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: existing channels only in V1 (SafetyScreen with reviewer account + agreementId, or CONTENT_NOTICE), operator finds the comment by agreement id and author; a structured pointer is a later package decided together with the production operator.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-4: Confirm that the comment is accepted ONLY inside the same command as the stars, so a star-only review (every old APK) can never gain a comment later.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Canon makes the review immutable and does not define edit; a later-added comment is an edit. Owner wording 'opciono ... posle zavrsenog posla' is satisfied by an optional field in the same submit.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: same command only, existing 7 reviews stay comment-less, REVIEW_ALREADY_SUBMITTED / REQUEST_ID_REUSED for any later attempt.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-5: Maximum length, counting unit and character rules for the comment.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Canon says only 'short' (L-017); no number exists; precedents run 140..6000 and none is a rule for reviews.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: 500 code points after btrim, octet_length <= 2000, LF allowed, CR/TAB/control/bidi/zero-width characters rejected (ZWJ and variation selectors allowed), reject instead of silently normalising, server-enforced and CHECK-enforced, client counter.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-6: Apply the deterministic contact-data floor (ru4b_public_floor_reason) to review comments (reject phone numbers, e-mails, links, @handles)?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Canon states the floor for Q&A only; owner banned AI moderation and paid services, not deterministic validation; the floor misses spelled-out numbers and obfuscated addresses and cannot detect addresses, names or insults.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: apply it (privacy-minimising, deterministic, no provider), one plain-Serbian refusal code, documented residual risk; no AI classifier.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-7: Feed scope - list only reviews that carry a comment (default) or every eligible review as D-0128 literally says; Requester profile only or both profiles; account-level list; where does the reviewed person read comments about themselves?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: D-0128 literally names the Requester profile; the functional audit put the individual review feed in later scope unless selected; listing legacy star-only reviews would retroactively expose attributable ratings given under the aggregate-only promise; own public profile has no route today. Blocks the APPLICATION and the client, not the candidate.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: separate paged reader, list only commented reviews, one account-level list usable from both profile kinds, gated exactly like rpc_get_public_profile, own comments reachable through the own profile section; stars/count/average unchanged.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-8: Re-confirm reviewer identity disclosure (D-0129: public avatar + name, tap to reviewer profile) and accept immediate publication with no blind or delayed reveal (F144).
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: F144 forbids inventing a blind/simultaneous model; free text raises retaliation exposure; serious-privacy permissions are owner decisions (AGENTS 3.1.1). Blocks the APPLICATION only.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: keep D-0129 as locked, publish with the stars at submit time, no deadline, state the retaliation risk in the approval block as a conscious acceptance.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-9: Block and closure rules for TEXT - author blocked by the subject, subject or author closure-restricted, comment written about a restricted target.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Stars deliberately survive blocks and may be written about a restricted target (tested canon behaviour); for public free text the same rule lets a blocked person publish about the blocker; F156 forbids inventing an opposite block rule.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: keep write behaviour identical to stars (no refusal that would reveal a block) and hide the comment at READ time while the pair is blocked or the author/subject is closure-restricted.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-10: Closure disposition - author closes: erase the comment (default, regardless of Agreement protection like chat messages); subject closes: hide-not-erase (default) or erase on either side.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: CL-4/AF-D22 imply erasure of the author's free text; LEG-10 decision 8 and the AF22 inventory ownerScope ('reviewer OR target') leave the subject-closure case open; protected-Agreement handling differs between messages (erased) and responses (skipped).
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: author closure deletes the comment row via the certified executor; subject closure hides but retains; protected Agreement does not stop the erasure; no retention number invented.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-11: May Dogovori completed by 48h auto-completion or confirmed after a reported problem receive a comment (same gate as the stars)?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Skeptic correction R07: COMPLETED covers both paths and there is no review window; a stricter gate would be invented policy.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: same gate as stars, no deadline (do not reuse the 48h window).

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-12: Export - include the author's own comment in ownAgreementReviews and exclude comments received about a person?
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Export is authored-only today; received text is third-party content and a copy beyond the author's closure; export cannot run on DEV until a policy is published.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: own comment included (count stays 52, projection V5_9 -> V5_10), received comments excluded, updated EXPORT_PROJECTION.md.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-13: Privacy classification, lawful basis, DPIA need, retention period for review comments, and the update of the legal and store drafts that currently say no free-text review exists.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Legal/privacy texts and retention periods are owner/legal inputs (AGENTS 3.4.5); LEG-09 P-19/G-10, LEG-10 decision 8 and DPIA [[PROVERITI]] are open; store UGC rules are release gates. Does not block the DEV candidate or the DEV apply.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: classify as user-authored personal content under the existing class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS, no number for retention, update the drafts in the same package, keep store/legal readiness unclaimed.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-14: Edit and delete of a review or comment.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: NOT DEFINED by the canonical product (immutable review, F144 open); the owner allows it only if canon already defines it.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: NOT DEFINED - owner decision; ship V1 immutable, no author edit, no author delete; only closure erasure and (if approved) moderation hide remove text.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-15: Old-client mechanism - new function names (recommended) versus in-place replacement of the 5-argument function.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Engineering choice disclosed to the owner: in-place replacement risks PGRST203/unproven resolution and breaks pinned proofs; new names keep every legacy pin intact.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: rpc_submit_agreement_review_v2 + rpc_get_my_agreement_review_v2, legacy functions byte-identical, capability gate in the client; in-place replacement only with a real-PostgREST proof.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-16: Tags - leave the live tag catalog untouched although final canon calls tags superseded.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: Source/DEV keep 6 tags (4 of 7 reviews carry tags); changing the catalog or version breaks every installed review screen.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: untouched; record the canon disagreement for a separate decision.

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-17: Vocabulary, notification and draft rules - 'ocena' for star counts and 'komentar' for text; notification copy unchanged (no rating, no text, no 'ti' rewrite of stored text); draft kept in memory only with a Back confirm.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: The UI already uses 'recenzija' for the star count; notification matrix allows rating only if policy allows; persisted drafts contradict the safety-screen rule that content never goes to local storage (C-25 corrected).
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: as stated; no new event type (the closed user_activity_events CHECK would change).

decisionsNeeded.question: D-DEC-18: Extra abuse limits - any per-account/per-day cap on comments, and whether to change AF-D17 (unlimited safety reports) for comment reports.
decisionsNeeded.whyOpen: No cap exists anywhere for reviews; a number would be invented policy; AF-D17 deliberately exempts safety channels; LEG-07 promises protection from report abuse.
decisionsNeeded.recommendedDefault: PROPOSAL: no new cap, no AF-D17 change; structural bound (one per review, completed Agreement only) plus validation; route comment reports through the throttled CONTENT_NOTICE where possible.

synth.recommendation: Build the D12 package as a SEPARATE-TABLE, additive, certificate-re-binding package, all PROPOSAL until the owner answers the two candidate-blocking decisions (D-DEC-2 moderation effect/operator, D-DEC-3 report pointer). Core design: a new private table private.agreement_review_comments_v1 keyed 1:1 to the existing immutable review (stars table, its trigger, its 7 rows and its input_hash formula stay byte-identical); NEW function names (rpc_submit_agreement_review_v2, rpc_get_my_agreement_review_v2, a gated keyset reader rpc_list_review_comments_v1, optionally a service-only moderation function) with every legacy review RPC left byte-identical so installed APKs keep working with no new error name; the comment rides on exactly the star gate (completed Agreement, one per side, atomic in the same command, immutable, no edit/delete because the canon defines none); deterministic validation only (500 code points, strict rejection, existing contact floor), no AI and no paid service; comment text never in push/payload/audit/logs; author-closure erasure through the certified executor (DELETE branch), subject-closure hide-not-erase pending decision, no retention number invented; own-comment export in the existing dataset (count stays 52, projection V5_10). Because the table and the three edited pinned closure functions move the closure digest 58447d77, the apply is one atomic statement with the three-place re-bind and needs the owner's explicit approval naming the re-bind; the revert refuses while any comment exists. Sequence: (1) owner answers D-DEC-2 and D-DEC-3 (the rest have safe defaults); (2) write the generator, candidate, revert and postflight test-first on a disposable chain extended with EX-04a-d; (3) prove old-client contract, parity, validation, gates, no-leak, export, real two-account closure, certificate re-bind, revert; (4) run the read-only DEV preflight (SQL above) immediately before; (5) present the separate approval block and ask for exactly 'PRIMENI D12 PISANI KOMENTAR' with the re-bind, retaliation acceptance (D-DEC-8) and legal-draft updates listed; (6) only after a clean DEV postflight build the client behind a DEV-workflow-only flag; native proof stays pending on two accounts on the HONOR. Do not claim D12 closed until the star-only native proof for the current build, the comment two-account proof, the report/moderation operator and the legal/retention inputs are each evidenced or explicitly deferred. Nothing was written, applied or called with a provider in this analysis.

mapped.area: Existing agreement review (ocena) model on the server: tables, columns, functions, policies, eligibility, uniqueness, idempotency, aggregates and client contract (read-only; DEV leqcwgzvjsxugfgzdmth, ledger 219)
mapped.summary: The star review is one immutable table, private.agreement_reviews (id, agreement_id, reviewer_account_id, target_account_id, rating 1..5, tags text[] from a fixed 6-code catalog (max 3), client_request_id, input_hash, created_at), reachable only through three SECURITY DEFINER RPCs: rpc_submit_agreement_review(uuid,uuid,jsonb,jsonb,uuid), rpc_get_my_agreement_review(uuid), rpc_get_account_reputation(uuid). A second reader is the public-profile trust block of rpc_get_public_profile. NO free-text field exists anywhere in the review model: no text column, no table, no UI TextInput, and the legal and store drafts state it explicitly. A review is created by either participant of an Agreement whose status and agreement_execution.state are both COMPLETED, only for the counterpart, once per (Agreement, reviewer) and so at most twice per Agreement, and it can never be edited or deleted (trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE plus client wording 'Uspesna ocena se ne menja'). Reputation is one account-level count and average (round(avg,2)), shown on the public profile and the own profile; app_profiles.rating_worker/rating_requester exist but nothing writes them (0 of 10 DEV profiles), so reviews do not feed matching. Live DEV bodies were read and equal the migrations plus the closure patch; ex04c (ratingDue/ratings) is applied (ledger 219). Package-relevant constraints found: (1) canon defines the review as immutable, so edit/delete must not be invented and a comment cannot be added later without a new decision; (2) any new column, constraint, trigger or table on the review table moves the closure certificate 58447d77 (isolated recertification plus owner approval), while function-only changes do not; (3) old clients decode the context strictly (tag catalog deep-equal) but tolerate extra keys, and the 5-argument submit signature must be replaced, not overloaded (PostgREST ambiguity); (4) no closure/erasure code, retention rule, moderation/report path or review list reader exists for reviews today; (5) the reputation reader has no same-world or relationship check, unlike the public profile.

findings.claim: Uniqueness: UNIQUE(agreement_id, reviewer_account_id) means at most one review per participant per Agreement, so at most two per Agreement (one per side); UNIQUE(reviewer_account_id, client_request_id) is the idempotency key; CHECK reviewer<>target. A reviewer reviews only the counterpart; a given account can be requester in one Agreement and worker in another and has ONE reputation across both roles. The only anti-spam bound is that uniqueness plus the Agreement-completion gate (no rate limit, no content filter exists, because there is no content). findings.claim: Eligibility to rate: the caller must be authenticated and be requester_account_id or worker_account_id of the Agreement (else REVIEW_NOT_ALLOWED); p_target_account_id must equal the counterpart (else REVIEW_NOT_ALLOWED; self-target gives REVIEW_INPUT_INVALID); agreements.status must be 'COMPLETED' AND an agreement_execution row for it must have state='COMPLETED' (else REVIEW_NOT_COMPLETED); the caller must have no review yet for that Agreement (else REVIEW_ALREADY_SUBMITTED). Agreement statuses are CONFIRMED/SUPERSEDED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED and execution states CONFIRMED/AWAITING_REQUESTER/COMPLETED/CANCELLED. COMPLETED is reached only when the requester confirms (rpc_confirm_completion) or the 48 h requester deadline expires with no problem opened (rpc_tick_auto_completion, service-only); the worker alone cannot complete. DEV: 8 Agreements = 4 COMPLETED, 3 CONFIRMED, 1 CANCELLED; all 4 COMPLETED also have execution COMPLETED.

findings.claim: Closure restriction is enforced in three places: (a) PostgREST pre-request hook pgrst.db_pre_request=public.rpc_closure_api_guard (set on role authenticator) raises ACCOUNT_CLOSING 42501 for every /rpc/* call of an authenticated caller in a restricted closure state (READY/EXECUTING/FAILED/CLOSED) except the closure/support allow-list; (b) trigger pre_v3_closure_review BEFORE INSERT calls private.closure_guard_owned_write('ACCOUNT','reviewer_account_id'), i.e. it checks only the REVIEWER; (c) rpc_get_my_agreement_review.eligible includes 'not private.closure_account_restricted(u)'. The counterpart being restricted does not block being reviewed (aggregate reads for them are hidden instead, see R12). An idempotent replay returns before the Agreement and insert checks. DEV has 1 closure request (state BLOCKED, not a restriction).

findings.claim: Idempotency: command key is (reviewer_account_id, client_request_id), serialized by pg_advisory_xact_lock('uskoci:review-command:<account>:<request>') and a second lock per (Agreement, reviewer). input_hash = sha256 of jsonb {agreementId, target, rating, tags(sorted)}. A repeat with the same request id and the same hash returns the stored receipt with idempotentReplay=true even after later blocks; the same request id with a different hash raises REQUEST_ID_REUSED 22023; a new request id for an already-reviewed Agreement raises REVIEW_ALREADY_SUBMITTED. Concurrent duplicates yield exactly one row (proof). Any text added to the command must keep the hash formula for comment-less input unchanged, otherwise stored rows would answer replays with REQUEST_ID_REUSED.
evidence: DEV SQL: live prosrc of rpc_submit_agreement_review (hash and lock lines)

findings.claim: Client decode contract (what installed APKs enforce): decodeReviewContext rejects the response unless tagCatalog.version === 'PRE_V3_REVIEW_TAGS_V1', maxTags === 3 and tagCatalog.tags deep-equals the 6 REVIEW_TAGS in order; eligible must be boolean, authoritative true, review and eligible cannot both be set; the receipt needs reviewId, agreementId, reviewerAccountId, targetAccountId, integer rating 1..5, tags subset of the catalog, clientRequestId, ISO createdAt, boolean idempotentReplay, authoritative true; after submit the screen re-reads the context and requires the same reviewId. Unknown extra keys are ignored (record()/field-wise checks), so additive keys are safe for old clients; changing the tag catalog or its version breaks them (REVIEW_INVALID_RECEIPT). The reputation decoder requires averageRating with at most 2 decimals; the public-profile mapper requires ratingAvailable/reviewsAvailable/reviewCount/ratingAverage to be mutually consistent.

Old-client safety of any signature change: PostgREST resolves named-argument RPC calls by name, so adding an optional comment parameter as a SECOND overload next to the 5-argument function would make the old 5-named-arg call ambiguous. The EX-04 S2 precedent (ex04b) replaced the 4-argument reader by DROPping it without CASCADE and creating the 5-argument one in the same statement. An alternative that keeps the existing signature untouched is a separate new RPC for the optional text. Also keep tagCatalog.version/tags and all existing keys byte-identical and add only new keys.
evidence: DEV SQL: exactly 1 overload each of rpc_submit_agreement_review, rpc_get_my_agreement_review, rpc_get_account_reputation

findings.claim: The canonical product already defines a submitted review as immutable (no edit, no delete): client wording 'Ovaj Dogovor je vec ocenjen. Uspesna ocena se ne menja.', DB trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE, registry D12 'Immutable review command', migration header 'immutable bilateral completed-Agreement reviews ... No public free text or reciprocal status.', and the export projection doc limits the export to own authored ratings/tags with 'no incoming review or reciprocal completion status'. Per the owner's rule, edit/delete must not be invented for the comment; the canon says none. The registry also keeps D12's comment as 'poseban, neprimenjen server/schema/privacy/moderation paket' with 'not_in_scope' in EX04 and an owner gate 'D12 pisani komentar: poseban server paket'.

Legal and store drafts currently state that NO free-text review comment exists, so D12 will make them wrong unless updated in the same package: LEG-09 processing register P-19 ('slobodan tekst komentara nije uveden'), release REVIEW_NOTES_DRAFT ('no free-text review comment exists (LEG-09 G-10)') and DATA_DECLARATIONS_DRAFT GS-23 ('no free-text review comments: G-10', user-generated-content row). AF22 closure inventory classifies private.agreement_reviews as proposedAction PSEUDONYM_MINIMUM, exceptionDependency SHARED_AGREEMENT, jsonCopyNotes 'Bounded tags, no free text'; LEG-10 row 9 says on closure 'ostaje pseudonimni minimum'.

Export covers only reviews AUTHORED by the requesting account: dataset catalog key ownAgreementReviews (data class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS, fields agreementId, createdAt, id, rating, tags; filter reviewer_account_id=REQUEST_ACCOUNT and participant of the Agreement). Reviews received are not exported. Both private.data_export_dataset_catalog() (md5 7fc01c56...) and private.data_export_snapshot(...) (md5 b198bff5...) reference the table, and the Voice B1 revert shows they are re-created as part of the certified closure/export function set. A text field would need an explicit catalog field, a snapshot projection change and a binding refresh.
evidence: DEV SQL: snippets of data_export_dataset_catalog and data_export_snapshot (ownAgreementReviews)

findings.claim: No executable closure, erasure or retention treatment of reviews exists in DEV code: retention class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS is registered (required, active) and mapped in private.closure_dataset_catalog_v5, but private.retention_policy_sets=0 and private.retention_policy_rules=0 (no period, no rule), no function whose name matches closure/erasure/redact references agreement_reviews, and the unconditional immutability trigger blocks any UPDATE/DELETE, so a closure program could not pseudonymize or erase a review row (or a future comment) without a deliberate trigger exception. The FK ON DELETE RESTRICT on both account ids also means the reviewer/target accounts are retained as subjects. LEG-10 open decision 8 (retention of the other side's reviews when one account closes) is unresolved.

findings.claim: Certificate coupling: private.closure_source_digest_v5() hashes, for EVERY public/private table, the columns (name, type, not-null), the constraints and the triggers (name, definition, trigger-function body md5). Adding a column, constraint or trigger to private.agreement_reviews, or creating any new table, therefore moves the certified digest (58447d77...) and needs the isolated recertification plus the owner's explicit approval; replacing function bodies in place (rpc_*, non-trigger helpers) does not move it (ex04c asserted this). Candidate designs that keep the review table untouched and add only functions would avoid recertification, but a comment needs storage somewhere, so a new table or column is expected to recertify.
evidence: AGENTS.md section 3.1.4 (any change that moves the certified closure digest needs recertification and owner approval)

findings.claim: Visibility gap for a future reader: the only existing cross-account review surface (rpc_get_account_reputation) has no same-world check and no relationship requirement, whereas rpc_get_public_profile applies ACTIVE-profile, closure, block and same-world cuts. DEV owner accounts live in the TEST world (pkg029e), so a new comment reader must reuse the public-profile cut, not the reputation reader's weaker cut. Also no per-review list or paging exists: a list reader needs an index such as (target_account_id, created_at desc, id) and a bounded page, because authenticated statement_timeout is 8 s.

findings.claim: Product questions not answerable from canon and not to be invented: who sees the comment (reviewed person only, or on the public profile as a list, and with the reviewer's name or anonymised), maximum length and allowed content, retention/pseudonymisation of a comment when the reviewer or the reviewed account closes (LEG-10 open decision 8; AF22 PSEUDONYM_MINIMUM with the SHARED_AGREEMENT exception), and how a reported comment is hidden given immutability (hide flag vs deletion). Today only the numeric aggregate is public and the counterpart cannot read the individual rating or tags.

openQuestions: Should the optional comment be accepted only inside the same immutable submit command as the stars (canon-consistent default), or may a comment be attached later to a star-only review? The latter contradicts REVIEW_IMMUTABLE and REVIEW_ALREADY_SUBMITTED and needs an explicit owner decision.

Where does the comment live: a new table (certificate recertification, new RLS/ACL, export and closure coverage) or a new nullable column on private.agreement_reviews (also moves the certified digest 58447d77 and needs a trigger exception for closure redaction)? Either way the closure certificate and export function set must be re-bound with the owner's approval.

Who may read the comment and where is it rendered (reviewed person only, public profile list, candidate cards), and is the author identified? Any list must reuse the rpc_get_public_profile visibility cut (ACTIVE, closure, block, same-world), not the weaker rpc_get_account_reputation cut.

mapped.area: PRIVACY, EXPORT, CLOSURE, RETENTION (D12 written review comment)
mapped.summary:
Read-only analysis. Repository sources and live canonical DEV (leqcwgzvjsxugfgzdmth, SELECT and catalog only, no review text or personal content read) agree on the following.

1. The canonical review model is immutable and text-free. private.agreement_reviews stores one row per (Agreement, reviewer) with rating 1-5 and at most 3 catalog tags. It has no text column. A trigger refuses every UPDATE and DELETE for every role. The public surface is the account-level count and average. Rating and tags are visible only in the reviewer's own receipt.

2. Closure today retains the whole review row. The table is in the closure dataset catalog (class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS) but not in the 75-relation redaction roster. The source inventory classifies it PSEUDONYM_MINIMUM / SHARED_AGREEMENT. No existing closure proof exercises it.

3. A comment cannot be built as function-only. Any storage for it, a column or a table, moves the closure source digest (live 58447d77..., ledger 219). So does any edit to the redaction roster functions (relations / scope / patch / exceptions). Both are required for the author-closure rule. D12 therefore needs the full certificate re-bind pattern of Voice B1: one atomic transaction, owner approval that names the re-bind explicitly, and a revert that refuses while comment data exists.

4. Export is cheap and certificate-neutral. It needs a catalog field, a snapshot projection edit and a projection version bump (V5_9 to V5_10). The export functions are not in the 88-function digest roster. Export is not operational on DEV anyway: the retention schedule, legal documents and processor map have 0 published rows.

5. Retention periods for ratings, tags and comments are NOT defined anywhere. AF-D22 gives only a shape: history stays while the account exists, personal and private content is erased or anonymized at closure, exception durations are unset. The LIVE plan says text needs its own contract, moderation and retention.

6. Several decisions are missing for the comment: audience and attribution, behaviour when the target closes, retention, classification and legal basis, export of received comments, a removal path given immutability, and contact-data leakage control without AI. They are listed as DECISION_NEEDED findings and open questions.

findings.claim: Personal content is classified through 15 required and active retention data classes. The live list equals the LEG-10 table. private.closure_dataset_catalog_v5 maps each class to relations. Reviews belong to class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS, whose only relation is private.agreement_reviews. The only tables outside the catalog are 18 global or config tables with no review content.

The closure Edge worker and the client accept a CLOSED set of exactly four exception reason codes (SCOPED_EVIDENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED, MEDIA_EVIDENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED, HISTORY_ATTRIBUTION_REVIEW_REQUIRED, SHARED_DECISION_REVIEW_REQUIRED), each with a client label. findings.claim: Certificate impact by change type, derived from the live digest sources and the Voice B1, EX-04 and B24 precedents. (a) Function-body-only change of a function that is neither in the 88-function roster nor a trigger function: digest unchanged. This holds for rpc_submit_agreement_review, rpc_get_my_agreement_review, rpc_get_account_reputation, account_reputation, rpc_get_public_profile and all data_export_* functions. EX-04 S1-S4 (ledger 216-219) did exactly this and asserted the digest unchanged. (b) A new column on an existing table: schema digest moves, and so does a CHECK on it. (c) A new table in public/private: both the schema digest and the program digest (its owner/ACL/RLS row) move. (d) Any edit of a roster function (closure_redaction_relations/scope/patch, closure_erasure_exceptions/blockers, rpc_start_account_closure_execution, support_reference_v5, the digest functions themselves): moves it. (e) Any body change of a trigger function on any public/private table, e.g. guard_review_immutable: moves the schema digest (trigger function md5 is hashed), and the program digest too if the table is a redaction relation. (f) Index, RLS policy, comment, default: unseen. Consequence: a comment can only be stored via (b) or (c) and its author-closure erasure needs (d) and (e), so D12 necessarily moves and re-binds the certificate. It cannot be function-only.

findings.claim: A re-bind is a privacy certification of the erasure program and needs the owner's explicit approval plus an isolated recertification. AGENTS 3.1.4 says so, and the B24 Part 2 and Voice B1 precedents applied it. Pattern: one atomic transaction; refuse unless the predecessor is ready and no closure is EXECUTING; change; prove the digest moved because of this change only (restore-and-compare inside the transaction); update closure_source_v5 and closure_erasure_source_v5; re-create retention_ai_source_ready() with the new sha; assert ready, binding present, and the readiness function changed only by its constant; delta accounting of all functions, tables, columns, constraints, triggers, policies and buckets. The owner's approval block for Voice B1 named the re-bind explicitly. The revert is a separate 'primeni' and refuses while any user data of the feature exists. Removing user data is 'a separate owner decision, never a side effect'. A D12 revert would therefore refuse once a first comment exists.

No retention schedule is published, so nothing executes by schedule. Live: 0 retention_policy_sets, 0 rules, 0 legal documents, 0 processor maps, 0 retention holds. The executors that exist are the AI abandoned-unbound purge (needs a published binding), the export-copy cleanup (needs the export binding) and the AF-D22 event-bound closure. Closure does NOT need a published schedule (binding has legalPolicyAttested:false). There is no general expiry executor, no later purge of retained pseudonymous records, and no rule for a never-closed (inactive) account.

The owner's retention decisions that DO exist. AF-D22 (2026-09-13): no automatic 30-day deletion of completed jobs, Agreements, messages or photographs; history stays while the account exists; no unconditional forever retention; at closure delete or anonymize personal and private content where applicable, with only necessary technical or legal exceptions; no exception duration invented. AF-D22 does not literally enumerate ratings, tags or comments (it names jobs, Agreements, messages and photographs), so applying it to review data is by analogy.

findings.claim: What canonical sources DEFINE for review data today. Only a participant of an Agreement with status COMPLETED and execution state COMPLETED may review the counterpart. One review per (Agreement, reviewer), so at most two per Agreement. Rating 1-5 integer; at most 3 distinct tags from a fixed catalog of 6. Immutable. Idempotent by client_request_id plus input hash. One ACCOUNT reputation (no role-specific cache), count and average rounded to 2 decimals. Rating and tags visible only in the reviewer's own receipt, so even the target sees only the aggregate and a fixed 'Nova ocena' notification. Public and profile reads are fenced by closure and by safety blocks. A block does not remove the review entitlement. A restricted reviewer cannot insert. Retention class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS. Own-authored export. Closure retains the row.

The canonical text on written comments, all consistent: 'Pisani komentar ima zaseban server/privacy/moderation ugovor i odvojeno prihvatanje'; 'Tekst zahteva poseban ugovor, moderaciju i retention; ne proglasiti ga gotovim uz postojeće zvezdice'; 'bez izmišljene javne reputacije'; 'Pisani komentari ocena uslovni, ne polje ubačeno radi bogatijeg ekrana'. The table migration header says 'No public free text or reciprocal status', and its table comment says 'No text column'. These predate the owner's 2026-10-01 D12 decision, which supersedes them under AGENTS section 1 item 1 ('latest explicit owner decision wins'). The table comment must be updated by the package. The D12 decision does not itself authorise application ('PRIMENI D12 PISANI KOMENTAR').

Audience, attribution and surface of a comment are undefined. Today no per-review content is shown to anyone but the reviewer, only count and average. Closure disposition of a comment when its TARGET closes is undefined. Derivable default: author closes means the comment is erased (CL-4, CZ-3) and the rating and tags remain as pseudonymous minimum. Target closes: counterpart-authored content normally stays (LEG-08 s6; scope-by-author precedent), and the closed account's reputation is already hidden. But this text is about the closing person and may contain their personal data, and the CL-4 free-text rule does not say who must decide. Erasing text on the subject's closure would be a new precedent (scope t.target_account_id), so it needs an explicit owner decision.

Removal, correction and legal erasure of one comment are not possible under the canonical immutable model. The trigger blocks everyone and edit/delete is not defined, so D12 must stay immutable per the owner's 'only if canonical defines it' constraint. But LEG-02 section 23 and LEG-05 section 11 promise that the platform 'može ukloniti ili ograničiti ocenu', LEG-04 section 15 promises rectification/erasure through support, and LEG-07 section 11 says a report 'ne briše sam sadržaj ni recenziju'. A removal or hide path (certified exception or a state column, both moving the certificate) needs an owner decision and a moderation actor (LEG-14 not started).

additions.claim: Old-client breakage by overload: rpc_submit_agreement_review exists as exactly ONE function with the 5-argument signature (uuid,uuid,jsonb,jsonb,uuid). Adding the optional comment as a 6th parameter via a plain CREATE FUNCTION creates a second overload; a named-argument call carrying only the five old keys then matches both candidates (the second via its default) and is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 'function is not unique' / PostgREST PGRST203 class), which would break the rating submit of every installed APK. Safe shapes: replace the function in ONE statement (drop the 5-arg signature without CASCADE and create the same name with p_comment text default null, re-granting EXECUTE to authenticated as ex04b did for rpc_list_my_applications_page) or add a differently named RPC and leave the old one untouched. The disposable proof must call the old 5-key payload through the real PostgREST path after install. The PostgreSQL ambiguity is the standard behaviour but was NOT reproduced by me against DEV (no DDL allowed).

mapped.summary:
The repo already has a private, account-keyed report and block system and a single-operator support-case system. Both stop at the person or at a message. Nothing can name a review, and nothing can hide, remove or sanction content. No code, DEV state or provider was changed: only read-only SELECT and catalog queries on canonical DEV plus repo reads. All counts and catalog facts, no personal content.

REUSABLE UNCHANGED (verified live, none in the certified set)
- rpc_submit_safety_report: report a person with an Agreement or Need context and free text. It is not suppressed by a block.
- rpc_set_account_block and the block pair-guard: hides the pair's profiles and reputation from each other and suppresses deliveries.
- rpc_read_safety_target and the client report entry on public profiles.
- Support topic CONTENT_NOTICE, labelled 'Prijava sadržaja ili recenzije', with a free-text description only.
- private.ru4b_public_floor_reason(text): a deterministic email/link/@handle/phone floor, today used only for Q&A.
- private.location_private_text_valid(jsonb,int): multi-line text validator that rejects control characters.
- Idempotency, audit, event and closure-guard patterns, and the client text pipeline (trim, NFC, control and surrogate checks, code-point count).

NEW (not present today)
- Review text storage and validation. private.agreement_reviews has no text column and is immutable.
- A moderation state or action on a review. support_decisions_v5.effect is CHECK ('NONE'); no function sets profile_status SUSPENDED.
- A structured report-on-review reference (support evidence kind REVIEW or review_id on the report).
- Any reader that lists individual reviews. Only the reviewer's own receipt and the account aggregate exist.
- Review-specific abuse limits. The only volume bound is one review per Agreement per side.

AUTOMATIC MODERATION
- Exists only for task publication (uskoci-publication-evaluate) and Q&A (uskoci-qa-classify). Both are Gemini behind paid-test env flags.
- Does not exist for reviews, chat, profile text, support or reports.
- Nothing must be added. Reusing the Gemini path would be a paid call plus a new policy bundle.

TWO COUPLINGS TO THE CERTIFIED CLOSURE DIGEST
- The certified digest hashes 88 functions, including every support function, support_reference_v5, closure_support_source_fence_v5 and closure_erasure_exceptions_v5. A REVIEW evidence kind in support therefore moves it.
- closure_schema_digest_v5_139() hashes the columns, constraints and triggers of every public and private table. Any new column, table or trigger for comments or moderation moves it.
- The safety, block, review and public-profile functions are outside the 88, so function-only changes to them do not move it.

PRODUCT CANON ON REVIEW COMMENTS AND ABUSE
- L-017: 1-5 stars plus an optional short comment after a completed Dogovor.
- LIVE plan D12: text needs its own contract, moderation and retention.
- Closure plan W10: a moderation state on reviews, and a moderation change must affect the aggregates consistently.
- Open and not to be invented: review deadline, edit and blind or reciprocal reveal (F144); the maximum length of a 'short' comment; any hide, remove or sanction action (AF-D18 says a new public policy exception is a separate decision).

THE MODERATION PATH IS UNEXERCISED
- 0 safety reports, 0 blocks and 0 support cases on DEV.
- No active operator grant.
- N06, N07 and N08 are partial on the phone, with the report button never pressed.

findings.claim: Block versus a public comment: the source keeps the review entitlement for a blocked pair (a blocked reviewer can still submit), and the pair-block rule hides profiles from BOTH sides but not from third parties. A free-text comment written by someone the target has blocked would therefore be shown to everyone except the two people involved, with no existing rule for holding it. Canon F156 forbids inventing an opposite block rule, so what to do (publish, hold for operator, show only after unblock) is not decided anywhere.

findings.claim: RETALIATION / TIMING / EDIT-DELETE (owner-only, canon open): reviews are independent and bilateral with no reciprocal-reveal rule; F144 explicitly forbids inventing a blind-review model or a deadline; edit/delete is undefined in canon and the live behaviour is immutability. Owner must confirm (1) comments stay immutable (no edit/delete) as the existing implementation does, or define edit/delete; (2) whether any reveal-timing rule is wanted (default = none, as today); (3) how a moderation removal, if any, is represented without breaking immutability and D-0131's 'immutable review timestamp'. openQuestions: Who operates review-comment moderation after the private test? The support operator is a singleton with purpose PRIVATE_TEST_OWNER_SUPPORT and no active grant on DEV. Canon requires an operator, a queue, a status and a published contact (LIVE 13.3, APL-06), and D-0038 says fail closed until an authorized queue exists.

May a moderator hide, remove or restore a comment (a decision effect other than NONE)? AF-D18 and SUPPORT_CASE_API_143 say no support decision may change a review, and LEG-02 s.23 promises 'remove or limit'. W10 expects a moderation state that consistently affects the aggregates. This needs an explicit owner decision and an adapter.
Pre-publication hold (D-0038 fail closed) or publish-then-report for the comment?
Maximum length of the 'short' comment. No canonical number exists; existing text limits run 140 to 6000.

Apply the deterministic PII floor (private.ru4b_public_floor_reason) to the public comment? The owner banned AI and paid moderation, but canon states the floor only for Q&A. It also misses spelled-out numbers, obfuscated addresses and U+202E/U+200B.

Confirm that comments stay immutable (no edit, no delete), as REVIEW_IMMUTABLE and the client copy do today. Canon F144 leaves edit, deadline and blind or reciprocal reveal undefined and forbids inventing them.
A reviewer the target has blocked can still submit (source comment, proof line 126). Should that comment be published, held, or shown only after unblock? F156 forbids inventing a block rule.

Report-system abuse: AF-D17 exempts safety reports and blocks from quotas, but LEG-07 promises protection against report abuse. Add a safety-report quota or de-duplication, or route comment reports only through the throttled CONTENT_NOTICE topic?

How is the report pointer to a review modelled? Options: REVIEW kind in support references (certified functions, recertification), review_id on private.safety_reports (schema digest moves), or free-text only (CONTENT_NOTICE / safety narrative, no recertification).

Review model reconciliation, for the sibling areas: the 50-row reconciliation says 'tags superseded, input is only 1-5 + optional short comment', but the live model has a tag catalog and unique(agreement_id, reviewer_account_id) (the 'one per side' rule). Do comment and tags coexist?

Retention of moderation records after closure (LEG-10 questions 5 and 8) is undecided, and AGENTS 3.4.5 forbids inventing periods. The comment package must declare 'retained until the owner sets the schedule', as the existing review and report tables do.
