additions.claim: A4 installed-client breakage points. (1) Support read decoders are exact-key strict (src/data/supportCaseReadDecoders.ts:53-79): a case whose context or evidence snapshot has kind REVIEW (or any new key) decodes to null in an old APK. A REVIEW evidence kind in support would break the inbox or detail of the affected account in old builds. (2) reviewsClientService.decodeReviewContext requires JSON.stringify(tagCatalog.tags) to equal the built-in REVIEW_TAGS, and rejects a context where review is non-null and eligible is true. So the tag catalog must not change, and eligible must be false once a star review exists, even if a comment could still be added. It tolerates extra keys in receipts. (3) mapPublicProfile and the reputation decoder tolerate extra keys but require rating or count consistency (reviewCount, average and ratingAvailable must agree), so a public profile that adds a comment list must keep those fields consistent.

A5 closed-author dead end for reporting. After a reviewer's Auth producer is dispatched, (a) a new safety report naming that account is refused (BEFORE INSERT support_safety_closure_v5 -> support_safe_exit_v5 raises ACCOUNT_CLOSING for either party), and (b) support_allowed_actions_v5 returns an empty action list for any case involving that account, so the case author cannot reply or appeal. If the comment is retained (A1), a victim of an abusive retained comment from a closed author has only a fresh CONTENT_NOTICE case (free text, quota-limited) as a route. Hiding or removing the comment would still need the missing moderation action (M24).

mapped.area: CLIENT, UX AND OLD CLIENTS (D12 written comment with the star rating)
mapped.summary: Read-only trace of the rating flow, the public/own reputation display, notifications and every RPC shape the installed clients use (all builds since 2026-09-12, including APK 93e48799 built from bf48a5db and the legacy 11574c02 baseline, share the same review call shape; the review service files have not changed since 74f514d7 on 2026-09-25). Main conclusions. (1) Old clients survive an OPTIONAL comment parameter and new response keys unchanged, because every decoder reads named keys only and ignores extras; they break only if invariants change (tagCatalog version/maxTags/tags, eligible/review coupling, reputation reviewCount/averageRating/state, public-profile trust coupling, ratingDue/ratings aggregate, inbox target kinds, exact push title/body pairs). The one real structural risk is how the new parameter is introduced: the live function is a single overload `rpc_submit_agreement_review(uuid,uuid,jsonb,jsonb,uuid)` called by every installed client, so the EX-04 precedent (DROP old signature, CREATE new, justified there because nothing called the old one) is NOT automatically safe here and needs a disposable proof through real PostgREST with the exact 5-key body. (2) The current screen machinery cannot host a free-text field safely: any non-ok submit freezes the command and locks editing (useOwnedEditor has no settledFailure, attemptRef is never released), unknown server error names become a generic unknown-outcome message, and a successful save is rejected if the server normalizes the text differently from what the client sent. These are client requirements regardless of server design. (3) There is no place anywhere in the app where a written review could appear today: no review list on any profile, the recipient cannot read what was given about them, the notification resolves to the Dogovor (not the profile, as the UX draft proposed), and there is no structural report path for a review (Support has no review reference kind, Safety has no content category). (4) The canonical rule that a saved rating never changes ("Sačuvana ocena se ne menja", trigger pre_v3_review_immutable live) means the only canonically defined shape is: comment travels atomically with the stars in the same command; any later add/edit/delete is an owner decision, not something to design in. (5) Several product decisions the client depends on are still open (publication timing vs retaliation, author attribution, recipient visibility, draft persistence, wording of the who-sees-it disclosure). Nothing was written, applied or called with a provider; live checks were SELECT/catalog only, counts only, no review text. No HONOR/emulator evidence was gathered (not in scope); PostgREST overload/default behaviour is a proof obligation, not a measured fact.

findings.claim: All installed clients decode by named keys and ignore extras, and the tests pin this on purpose ('strips reciprocal/private extras'): a success receipt carrying extra keys returns only the whitelisted fields, a context with an extra top-level key returns the clean context, a reputation with extra role averages returns only the five known fields, and mapPublicProfile reads only named keys of the profile and of `trust`. So ADDING an optional return key (for example `comment` in the receipt, `commentMaxLength` in the context, a comment count in reputation) is invisible to every installed build. The flip side: the NEW client must add `comment` to its decoder whitelist explicitly or it will silently drop it.

findings.claim: How the optional comment parameter is introduced is the single structural old-client risk. Installed clients call the 5-key body. If the server DROPs the 5-arg function and CREATEs a 6-arg one whose sixth parameter has DEFAULT NULL, the old body should still resolve (PostgREST named-argument calls with defaults) - but this is a proof obligation, not a measured fact here. If the server instead adds a 6-arg overload and keeps the 5-arg one, the 5-key call matches both candidates and PostgREST can answer PGRST203 (ambiguous), which every installed client would map to the generic 'Ishod radnje nije potvrđen' unknown-outcome state on a plain star rating. The EX-04 S2 precedent (DROP the 4-arg function and CREATE the 5-arg one in one atomic statement) was only justified because 'nothing calls it on DEV or in src/'; that justification does NOT hold for this RPC, which every installed client calls. Also a replaced function must keep `authenticated`-only EXECUTE and is part of the certified function set (digest 58447d77) - the proof must therefore call it through real PostgREST with the exact body of reviews-authority.test.ts:17 against the replaced function and against the old client builds' decoders.

findings.claim: The rating screen cannot host a free-text field as built: ANY non-ok submit result is treated as an unknown outcome. useOwnedEditor.save sets reconcileRequired and uncertain unless the caller passes a narrow `settledFailure` predicate, and AgreementReviewScreen passes none; additionally it freezes the command (attemptRef.current = command; setAttempt) BEFORE the request and never clears it, so `editable = enabled && eligible && !attempt` becomes false for good and the person sees 'Čuvamo tvoj prvobitni izbor dok proveravaš ishod slanja.' with buttons 'Proveri sačuvanu ocenu' / 'Ponovi istu ocenu'. For stars and tags this is harmless (they cannot be wrong after client validation). For a comment that the server refuses deterministically (too long, forbidden content, not allowed) the person would be stuck with a rejected text that can only be replayed unchanged. The new client must distinguish deterministic refusals (pass settledFailure for the new codes, release attemptRef/attempt, keep the text editable, show the specific message) from unknown outcomes (keep the freeze and replay-identical-command behaviour). This is the same gap the earlier round recorded and skipped ('A deterministic refusal after an unknown outcome can only be replayed ... a follow-up').

findings.claim: Readback equality will fail on a successful save unless client and server agree on text normalization. The client accepts a submit receipt only if what the server echoes equals what the client sent (today: rating and JSON-equal tags). A comment would need the same check; if the server trims, collapses whitespace, normalizes line endings or Unicode form and the client compares the raw typed text, the save succeeds but the screen reports 'Potvrda radnje nije stigla cela. Osveži prikaz pre ponovnog pokušaja.' (REVIEW_INVALID_RECEIPT). The app already has two text conventions to align with: length counted in code points after trim ([...x.trim()].length; Array.from(x).length), NUL and lone surrogates rejected. The count unit, the limit and the normalization must be one rule written into both the server contract and a shared client helper.

findings.claim: Canonical product rule: a saved rating never changes. The immutability is enforced (trigger pre_v3_review_immutable on UPDATE/DELETE, live), spoken to the user ('Sačuvana ocena se ne menja.' and error REVIEW_ALREADY_SUBMITTED 'Uspešna ocena se ne menja.'), and the LIVE D12 card forbids inventing an edit ('ne uvoditi edit ocene zbog dizajna'). Consequence for the client: the only canonically defined shape is that the comment is sent atomically in the same command as the stars and shown after the same own-review readback. A comment added later to an already saved rating, an edit, or a delete is NOT defined by the canonical product and must not be designed in without an owner decision (the owner's message permits edit/delete only if the canonical product already defines it). Clients that cannot send a comment (all installed builds) will leave 'no comment' on their Dogovori forever, which is acceptable under this rule.

findings.claim: The comment text must never enter a notification, push or event payload, and the notification copy must stay byte-identical for old clients. The shared push copy contract states 'No user-authored text or entity data enters this function'; the foreground admission compares title/body against a frozen whitelist (a changed copy such as 'ocena i komentar' is silently dropped by installed builds); the review proof asserts no REVIEW_RECEIVED event with a non-empty payload. findings.claim: Publication timing versus the existing 'no reciprocal status' contract. The server contract deliberately never discloses whether the counterpart has reviewed (client tests assert it; migration header: 'No public free text or reciprocal status'; the screen report says 'Ratings revealed only once both sides have rated: a business rule, unchanged'). A public written comment can reveal that the other side has already reviewed, and can invite retaliation if the recipient has not yet rated. The owner must decide whether a comment is visible immediately, only after both sides rated, or after a delay; the client cannot decide this and must render only what the server returns, without inferring or announcing 'the other side reviewed' anywhere (including in the notification, which today carries no such fact).

findings.claim: Author attribution and role scope of a displayed comment decide the whole report UX. Reputation is keyed by ACCOUNT, not by role ('No role-specific rating cache'; the owner decided report/block are keyed by account because 'a person shows two faces'), while a public profile is per role (REQUESTER or WORKER profile id). findings.claim: No reusable text-moderation or contact-detail filter exists on DEV for free text shown to another person. A catalog search of public/private functions for names containing contact/pii/profan/moderat finds only rpc_reveal_contact and rpc_set_contact_grant; no function raises an error code containing CONTACT/PHONE/EMAIL/LINK/URL for user text; the pre-selection question RPCs use disposition (human) handling, not a text filter, and contain no regular expressions. The PKG-029 note 'Showing free text to the other party needs the same contact filter as questions' therefore does not point at an existing reusable filter. Consequence for the client: if the server adds a content refusal, its error name and Serbian copy are new work; if it adds none, the client must not pretend to filter (no invented client-side rule), and the report path of C-23 is the only abuse control. No automatic AI moderation and no paid service are allowed without separate approval (owner message).

Decision for the owner/product: in-memory with a confirm on Back, or a persisted per-account per-Dogovor draft (cleared on a saved review or when the Dogovor stops being eligible).

findings.claim: Export, closure and legal artifacts the client touches or that now contradict the shipped behaviour. (1) The data-export client treats the artifact as opaque bytes (<= 8 MiB, sha256/md5/length verified) and accepts only the six known descriptor keys, so adding review text to the export is invisible to installed builds but must not add descriptor keys and must keep the artifact under DATA_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES. The closure inventory only PROPOSES the action: AF22_CLOSURE_INVENTORY_144.json relation private.agreement_reviews has proposedAction PSEUDONYM_MINIMUM, exceptionDependency SHARED_AGREEMENT, jsonCopyNotes 'Bounded tags, no free text'; LEG-10 row 9 says 'zatvaranje: ostaje pseudonimni minimum' and open question 8 asks the retention period of the other side's ratings. All three row FKs (agreement_id, reviewer_account_id, target_account_id) are ON DELETE RESTRICT, so the row and any text in it outlive a hard account delete, and the unconditional guard_review_immutable trigger refuses an erasure UPDATE. A free-text column therefore needs: allowlist entry + scope clause + patch/allowed policy for the text column, a changed or bypassed immutability guard, an inventory change from 'no free text', and a decision on whose comment (author or subject) is erased when either account closes.
evidence: SQL: select prosrc of private.closure_redaction_scope_v5 and private.guard_review_immutable; pg_proc scan for '%agreement_reviews%' returned only account_reputation, data_export_snapshot, rpc_get_my_agreement_review, rpc_home_attention, rpc_list_my_agreements_page, rpc_submit_agreement_review

additions.claim: Old-client replay hazard at the cutover through the input hash. The live submit function computes input_hash as sha256 of jsonb_build_object('agreementId','target','rating','tags') only and answers REQUEST_ID_REUSED when a stored row for the same (reviewer, client_request_id) has a different hash. If the replacement adds a 'comment' key to the hashed object even when it is null, an installed client replaying a command whose first attempt landed before the swap (lost acknowledgement, the case the client is built for) would get REQUEST_ID_REUSED ('Zahtev je već upotrebljen...') instead of the idempotent replay. Rule: include the comment in the hash only when it is present, and prove in the disposable chain that the hash of a comment-less command is byte-identical to the stored hashes of the 7 existing rows and to the hash the old function produces.
evidence: SQL: pg_get_functiondef(public.rpc_submit_agreement_review) - h:=encode(extensions.digest(jsonb_build_object('agreementId',...,'target',...,'rating',...,'tags',to_jsonb(tags_value))::text,'sha256'),'hex'); if found then if r.input_hash<>h then raise exception 'REQUEST_ID_REUSED'

additions.claim: Block does not stop the written comment. The live submit function deliberately keeps the entitlement for a blocked pair ('A block cannot remove the counterpart's completed-work review entitlement'). With stars only this was harmless; with free text a person the other side has blocked can still publish text about them on a public profile that third parties read. Block and closure checks only hide the pair from each other (public profile returns null, reputation raises REPUTATION_NOT_AVAILABLE). The owner must decide whether text is allowed for a blocked pair (stars yes / text no is a possible split), and the same for an author whose account is in closure. Not inventable by the client or the package.

mapped.summary: The canon already contains the product requirement for the comment, but not the contract. OWNER_LOCKED L-017/16-of-21 (2026-09-02): 1-5 stars plus an optional short text comment after a completed Dogovor, no multi-axis form. Locked display rules (D-0128..D-0131, F138-F141, J23) put individual reviews (stars + the real comment when present, reviewer avatar/name, relative age) beneath the average/count on the public profile, fed by the same eligibility/moderation truth as the aggregate. The canon explicitly leaves OPEN: review deadline, edit, publication timing (no blind/simultaneous model; do not reuse the 48h completion window) and account-score-versus-role-views (F144, AUTHORITY_INDEX line 13, OPEN_DECISIONS), plus every number and operator detail (comment length, retention period, moderation operator and SLA); AF-D22 and D-0141 forbid inventing retention periods. Every canonical source that mentions the comment says it needs its own server/schema/privacy/moderation package with candidate + disposable proof before any writer or text box (LIVE 3.2/9.3/D12, registry D12/EX04 not_in_scope, runbook P7 item 10, PLAN.md, APPLICATION_APPROVALS, ROUND_36); product direction was already approved by the owner on 2026-09-24 but the apply still needs his exact word. Live DEV (ledger 219) has no text column (private.agreement_reviews: 9 columns, immutable by trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE, 7 rows), retention class AGREEMENT_REVIEWS is required+active but 0 retention policy sets are published, only 3 review/reputation RPCs exist (no individual-review feed), support topic CONTENT_NOTICE exists but the support-case reference vocabulary has no review object and support decisions are contractually unable to change a review. Edit/delete is NOT defined by the canon (the star review is immutable by trigger and by LIVE D12 'ne uvoditi edit ocene zbog dizajna'); it must stay out unless the owner decides. 21 DECISION_NEEDED items below carry a recommended default each; the most consequential are: comment length, publication timing/retaliation (F144), whether the public individual-review feed is now selected (functional audit had it as later scope; D-0128 literally names the Requester profile), reviewer identity disclosure, moderation effect (hide comment only vs whole review) and who operates moderation (nobody is assigned), closure/export/retention treatment of the comment, tags (superseded in canon but live in source), and the closure-certificate re-bind that a new personal-content column will probably require.

findings.claim: Source disagreement on TAGS. Final canon says tags are superseded ('Final V1 review input is only 1-5 + optional short comment'; AUTHORITY_INDEX 'no invented tags'), yet source and DEV implement up to three tags from a six-value catalog and the 1998-era 112 spec still says 'optional comment/tags'. Question: does the comment package keep tags, retire them, or leave them untouched? RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: leave tags exactly as they are in this package (no new contract, no removal) and record the canon disagreement for the owner; reason: removing a live column/catalog is a different package and the owner never ordered it, adding anything about tags would invent policy.

Maximum comment length and validation. Canon says only 'short' / 'bounded input'; no number exists anywhere. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: 500 characters after trim (Unicode-safe, with an octet cap), empty string normalised to NULL, no newlines beyond a small limit, control characters rejected, deterministic validation only, server-enforced with a client counter; reason: matches the existing 500-character bound used for the close-search reason, stays well below the 1000 application message and 2000 safety narrative / chat bounds, fits 'short' of L-017. The owner must confirm the number because the canon names none.

Publication timing / reveal model (F144). Canon forbids inventing a blind or simultaneous-reveal model. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: no blind model; the comment becomes part of the review at the same moment as the stars (same single immutable command), exactly as the star already counts in the aggregate at submit time; surface the retaliation risk (RK-01) to the owner as a conscious acceptance, not a hidden choice. Reason: it is the only option that adds no new rule and keeps feed/aggregate consistent.

Review window / deadline after completion. Canon: none, and the 48h completion window must not be reused. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: no deadline (current behaviour: eligible while the Agreement is COMPLETED and the own review is absent), so an old completed Agreement can still receive a review with comment; reason: any deadline is an invented policy; add one only on an explicit owner answer.

Edit and delete of the comment (and of the review). Not defined by the canon; the owner said not to invent it. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: NO edit and NO author delete in this package; the comment is part of the same immutable review (trigger REVIEW_IMMUTABLE stays); the only removals are account-closure redaction (AF-D22) and a moderation hidden state decided by the owner/operator. Reason: matches the existing immutable-star contract and 'ne uvoditi edit ocene zbog dizajna'; if the owner wants edit/delete he must state the rule (time window, count, what is visible after edit, history) and it becomes a follow-up package.

Is the public individual-review feed now selected, and for which profiles? The functional audit (owner-approved analysis) put 'individual public review history' in later scope unless explicitly selected; D-0128 locks it but literally for the REQUESTER public profile; D-0129/D-0130 and current canon section 8 say 'public profile'; the owner's 2026-10-01 sentence says 'tamo gde je to predvidjeno proizvodom'. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: treat the 2026-10-01 sentence as selecting the feed for BOTH account profiles (one account-level reader, because reputation is one account score and the profile RPC serves both roles), all eligible reviews newest first, keyset-paged, star-only rows included with stars + reviewer identity + relative age, comment shown when present; ask the owner to confirm the Uskocer (worker) profile explicitly. Reason: avoids a comment that is stored but nowhere readable and keeps aggregate and feed on one eligibility truth.

Who sees the comment, beyond the public profile: (a) the author (own receipt, own 'Poslate' view); (b) the reviewed person (V2 target has a 'Primljene' view; the current system shows the reviewed person only the aggregate plus a generic notification and exports no incoming reviews); (c) the counterpart's profile visibility for signed-in users only (public profile is not readable anonymously); (d) blocked pair and closed/restricted accounts. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: visible only to signed-in users who can already open that public profile; author sees own review in the receipt; reviewed person sees it through their own public profile (no separate 'Primljene' screen in this package unless the owner asks); blocked pair sees nothing (same rule as rpc_get_account_reputation); rows of closed/restricted accounts are not listed. Reason: reuses existing visibility fences instead of inventing new ones.
evidence: docs/implementation/legal-drafts-20260930/LEG-09_processing_register.md:52 (P-03 public profile visible to logged-in users only)

findings.claim: Reviewer identity disclosure on a comment. D-0129 (OWNER_LOCKED 2026-08-25) shows the reviewer's authorized public avatar and name; this predates the AGENTS 3.1.1 rule that serious-privacy permissions are owner decisions and the F144 blind-model question. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: confirm D-0129 as locked (reviewer shown with the same public projection used elsewhere, truthful fallback when unavailable) and do not add anonymity; reason: it is an explicit owner lock, changing it is an invention; but because it increases retaliation exposure (RK-01) ask the owner to re-confirm it in the D12 approval block.

Moderation effect: when a comment is judged to violate rules, is the whole review (stars + comment) removed from feed AND aggregate, or only the comment text hidden while the stars stay? Canon says feed and aggregate must move together on a real eligibility change, and the draft terms say a negative-but-legitimate review is not removable. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: hide the comment text only (a reversible hidden flag with reason code and audit, stars and count unchanged); full review removal only by a separate explicit owner decision. Reason: least destructive, keeps aggregate math untouched (no 'hidden star penalties', D-0069), and still satisfies 'feed and aggregate use the same truth' because the aggregate does not depend on the text.

Who operates moderation and under what limits. Nobody is assigned (LEG-14 not started; owner is the only operator in the private test); support decisions may not change a review; the owner forbids automatic AI moderation and paid services for this package. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: a service-role-only, audited hide/restore function usable by the owner as operator in DEV/private test, no SLA text, no auto-hide; production operator, response time and appeal path stay explicit owner inputs. Reason: gives a real, provable moderation path without inventing an operations promise, consistent with 'a report button without an owner is not finished operations'.

Report entry for a comment. Existing channels: safety report (person, five categories, keyed by account) and support topic CONTENT_NOTICE (no review reference kind). RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: an in-app 'Prijavi' on a comment that creates a CONTENT_NOTICE support case with a NEW server-snapshotted reference kind for the Agreement review (id only, server builds the snapshot, no client-provided text beyond the reporter's own reason), no automatic removal, one open report per reporter per review (anti-spam). Reason: uses the existing case lifecycle and J24 acceptance path; extending the reference vocabulary is a contract change the owner must approve with the package.

Abuse and spam blocking inside the comment. Natural limit already exists (one review per participant per completed Agreement, idempotent command). Content-level controls are not in the canon (no profanity/PII filter anywhere for chat or profile text; LEG-05 draft forbids threats, private data, hate speech, unfounded criminal accusation). The owner forbids AI moderation. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: deterministic checks only (length, trim, control characters, repeated-character floods), no keyword/AI classifier; an owner choice is needed on whether obvious phone numbers, e-mail addresses and URLs inside a review are rejected, flagged for the operator, or allowed; recommended: reject them with a plain-Serbian message because it is privacy-minimising and deterministic. Reason: avoids invented moderation policy while giving a defensible baseline for the store UGC question.

Privacy classification of the comment and policy text. The canon classifies ratings only (LEG-09 P-19: 'slobodan tekst komentara nije uveden'); the comment is third-party-visible free text that can contain personal data of the reviewer and the reviewed person. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: classify as user-authored personal content, shared between two participants and public to signed-in users, purpose 'trust and choice', never in push or AI context, never in logs; update LEG-04/LEG-05/LEG-09/DATA_DECLARATIONS/STORE_LISTING drafts in the same change so no text claims 'no free-text comments'. Reason: the drafts currently assert the opposite and legal/privacy wording is an owner decision.

Blocked pairs, closed and restricted accounts for comment visibility. Canon: block never erases reviews; source hides the reputation read between a blocked pair and for restricted accounts; the comment rule is unspecified. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: mirror rpc_get_account_reputation (blocked pair: feed hidden; closed/restricted reviewer or target: row not listed), and do not delete the stored comment because of a block. Reason: consistent with the existing fence and with 'block never erases reviews'.

Export of the comment. Today only authored ratings/tags are exported and incoming reviews are excluded; export generation is blocked until a retention policy exists. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: export the author's own comment text with the authored review; do NOT export comments received about the account (third-party content) unless the owner/legal reviewer decides otherwise; update the export catalog binding in the same package and prove it on a disposable subject. Reason: follows the existing 'authored only' rule (EXPORT_PROJECTION) and avoids exposing another person's words.
evidence: docs/current/USKOCI_OPERATIVNI_MASTER_PLAN_LIVE.html:3910-3935 (N09: policy activation and E2E still open)

findings.claim: Account closure and deletion treatment. Author closes: AF-D22 says delete or anonymize personal/private content at closure, while LEG-10 row 9 keeps 'pseudonymous minimum' for rating/tags of a shared Agreement and LEG-08 says 'kopije ocena' are removed. Target closes: LEG-10 open question 8 (retention of the other party's reviews) is unanswered. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: on author closure redact the comment text (NULL plus redaction marker, receipt-only audit) and keep the pseudonymised star row for aggregate integrity; on target closure stop showing the review publicly and keep the stored row under the same pseudonymous minimum; no retention period is chosen. Reason: free text is more identifying than a star, AF-D22 trigger is closure not a day count, and canon forbids inventing durations. This needs a closure-program change and the owner's approval for the recertification (RK-02).

Retention period for comments (and for the AGREEMENT_REVIEWS class generally). Canon: none approved, no invented duration, scheduler stays off until a complete policy set is published; DEV has 0 policy sets. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: the package states no number, keeps the class under the existing 'dok nalog postoji' + closure rule, and records 'retention period = owner/legal input (LEG-10 questions)'; moderation-hidden comments are retained (not purged) for the same unknown period. Reason: D-0141 item 5 and AGENTS 3.4.5 forbid inventing it.

Notification content when a review with a comment arrives. Matrix leaves 'rating only if product policy explicitly allows it'; UX nacrt says bell-only; source emits a generic event with formal address. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: push and bell carry only the neutral text ('Stigla ti je nova ocena') in 'ti' form, never the rating value nor the comment text, destination = reviewed person's profile/reviews area; one event per persisted review as today. Reason: global rule never to put user-authored text in a push; owner rule 'ti'. Changing the stored event copy is a server change that needs its own mention in the approval block.

Terms acceptance and legal publication before user-generated review text. No command requires acceptance of terms before creating UGC (sign-up says the legal documents are not yet published; AGENTS 3.5.2 keeps that honest line); Google UGC policy expects acceptance and Apple 1.2 expects filtering, reporting, blocking and published contact. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: do not gate the DEV package on legal publication, but list it as an explicit release gate (store/legal input) and do not claim store readiness; keep the honest sign-up wording. Reason: legal texts and operator data are owner inputs and must not be invented.

Old-client behaviour (engineering default, not an owner policy): keep rpc_submit_agreement_review(uuid,uuid,jsonb,jsonb,uuid) callable and behaviour-identical for old APKs (no comment -> NULL), add the comment through a new optional parameter or a new function so an old client never fails or loses its replay/receipt, make new response keys additive only, and let new clients degrade gracefully (field hidden) when the server lacks the capability. Deterministic conflicts use PT409, never 40001. Reason: S04 compatibility rules and the EX-04 additive-keys precedent. The owner should only be told, not asked, unless the approach changes a certified function body.

Account-level versus role-level display of the comment (F144 'zajednicki account score vs prikazi uloga'). Source already implements ONE account reputation across both roles (verified in P9 proof) and both public profile projections read it; canon D-0132/D-0136 add role-scoped completed COUNTS only. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: keep one account-level review list; show the Agreement role context only if the owner wants it (not in the canon). Reason: matches the shipped, proven design and avoids inventing a role split.

openQuestions: DN-01 Tags: canon says superseded, source/DEV keep up to three tags; keep untouched in D12 (recommended) or retire?
DN-02 Comment maximum length and validation rules (recommended 500 characters after trim, server-enforced, deterministic).
DN-03 Publication timing/reveal (F144): confirm no blind model, comment published with the stars, and accept the retaliation exposure (recommended).
DN-04 Review window: confirm no deadline after COMPLETED (recommended); do not reuse the 48h completion window.
DN-05 Edit/delete: confirm none in this package (recommended); if wanted, the owner must define window, count, history and visibility.
DN-06 Is the public individual-review feed selected now, and for both account profiles or only the Requester profile named literally in D-0128? (functional audit had it as later scope)
DN-07 Who sees the comment: signed-in users on the public profile, author's own receipt/Poslate, reviewed person via own profile, no separate Primljene screen (recommended); confirm.
DN-08 Re-confirm D-0129 reviewer identity (avatar + public name) on comments despite retaliation exposure.
DN-09 Moderation effect: hide comment text only (recommended) versus remove the whole review from feed and aggregate.
DN-10 Moderation operator and limits: owner-only audited hide/restore, no SLA, no auto-hide, no AI (recommended); who is the production operator is an owner input (LEG-14 not started).

DN-11 Report entry: CONTENT_NOTICE case with a new server-snapshotted Agreement-review reference kind, no auto-removal, one open report per reporter per review (recommended); this extends the support-case contract.
DN-12 Abuse/spam: deterministic validation only; decide whether phone numbers, e-mails and URLs inside a review are rejected (recommended), flagged, or allowed.

DN-13 Privacy classification and policy text: classify as user-authored personal content, never in push/AI/logs, and update LEG-04/05/09 and store declarations that currently say no free-text review comment exists.
DN-14 Comment visibility for blocked pairs and closed/restricted accounts: mirror the reputation fence (recommended).

DN-15 Export: own authored comment included, received comments excluded (recommended); needs export catalog re-binding and a disposable proof; export generation is blocked until a retention policy exists.

DN-16 Closure: redact author's comment text at author closure and keep pseudonymised stars; behaviour when the reviewed person closes (LEG-10 question 8); requires closure-program change and certificate re-bind approval.
DN-17 Retention period: none approved; package states no number (recommended); owner/legal input.
DN-18 Notification content: neutral 'ti' copy, no rating value and no comment text, one event per review (recommended); bell-only (UX nacrt) versus push (matrix) divergence.
DN-19 Terms acceptance/legal publication/store UGC requirements as an explicit release gate, not a DEV blocker (recommended).
DN-20 Old clients: keep the 5-argument signature and behaviour unchanged, additive keys only, new optional parameter or new function (engineering default; inform the owner).

findings.claim: Live review store is one table, private.agreement_reviews (7 rows), with columns id, agreement_id, reviewer_account_id, target_account_id, rating (1..5), tags text[], client_request_id, input_hash, created_at. There is NO text column. Constraints: PK; UNIQUE(agreement_id,reviewer_account_id); UNIQUE(reviewer_account_id,client_request_id); CHECK reviewer<>target; CHECK input_hash sha256 hex; CHECK rating 1..5; CHECK private.review_tags_valid(tags) (catalog of 6 tags, max 3, distinct); three FKs ON DELETE RESTRICT (agreements, app_accounts x2). Index agreement_reviews_target_rating_idx(target_account_id) INCLUDE (rating). RLS enabled AND forced with 0 policies; relacl={postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres} only; no column ACLs; owner postgres; not in any publication; authenticated/anon/service_role have no USAGE on schema private and no table privileges. findings.claim: What moves the closure certificate (read from the live function definitions): private.closure_schema_digest_v5_139() hashes columns, constraints and triggers (with the md5 of each trigger function) of EVERY table in public and private plus storage.objects; private.closure_erasure_program_digest_v5() hashes the metadata and body md5 of 88 pinned functions (plus every trigger function on the closure redaction relations), the owner, relacl, RLS and force-RLS flags of EVERY public/private table, and the enabled state of every trigger; private.closure_source_digest_v5() combines the two with the sha of the surfaces and the md5 of the same 88 bodies. Consequence for D12: ANY storage for comment text (a new column or constraint on private.agreement_reviews, or a new table), any new trigger or trigger-function change, any ACL change on a public/private table, and any edit of a pinned function moves the digest and therefore requires the isolated three-place re-bind plus the owner's explicit approval. A function-only change to functions outside the 88 (and plain indexes, policies, data rows) does not move it, as EX-04 S1-S4 asserted. The pinned list includes closure_redaction_relations_v5/scope_v5/patch_v5/allowed_v5, closure_blockers_v5, closure_erasure_binding_v5, support_reference_v5, rpc_support_find_context_v5, rpc_review_account_closure_execution, rpc_start_account_closure_execution, rpc_closure_api_guard and both digest functions. Not in the 88: rpc_submit_agreement_review, rpc_get_my_agreement_review, rpc_get_account_reputation, rpc_get_public_profile, all data_export_* functions, closure_guard_owned_write (but its trigger bindings are hashed).

findings.claim: Comment text must never leak into the surfaces that currently carry a generic review signal. The proof asserts REVIEW_RECEIVED events have payload '{}' (reviews_authority_proof.mjs:59,144), the inbox item contains no tag text (:64), the push copy is the fixed string 'Stigla ti je nova ocena' / 'Pogledaj novu ocenu saradnje.' (supabase/functions/_shared/pushNotificationCopy.mjs:26) and the audit row for AGREEMENT_REVIEW_SUBMITTED carries only reviewId. A text-bearing design must keep these three surfaces text-free, keep input_hash content-derived and redactable, and keep the export free of the other person's content. Any new deterministic conflict must raise errcode PT409, never 40001 (PostgREST 14 retries 40001 without end, AGENTS.md:92); the current review functions already avoid 40001.

findings.claim: Storage shape is a design decision with equal certificate consequence: (A) a nullable text column on private.agreement_reviews (existing 7 rows stay NULL, one row per side, but the immutable trigger and the closure carve-out must be extended and the table's immutability contract changes from 'no text column'), or (B) a separate table keyed to the review (new table: owner, ACL, RLS, trigger, FK and constraint entries all enter both digests, and it must be added to the redaction relations and the AGREEMENT_REVIEWS dataset relations). Both move closure_schema_digest_v5_139 and closure_erasure_program_digest_v5 and need the owner's explicit approval of the re-bind. The package cannot be function-only.

Owner/legal decisions the live evidence cannot supply and the package must not invent: (1) behaviour and retention of a comment when the REVIEWED person's account closes (LEG-10 open decision 8; the AF-22 inventory scope includes target_account_id=CLOSING_ACCOUNT), while author closure is covered by AF-D22 erasure; (2) whether comments written ABOUT a person appear in that person's data export (today the proof asserts the peer review is excluded); (3) moderation effect and operator: support decisions are hard-limited to effect NONE, so 'hide/unlist after a report' needs an explicit owner-approved mechanism and who may use it, without automatic AI moderation or a paid service; (4) which public face (requester or worker profile) represents the author on a public review, given reputation is keyed by ACCOUNT (AGENTS.md:66) and F140 shows avatar/name; (5) whether a comment is allowed on a Dogovor that was auto-completed by rpc_tick_auto_completion without requester confirmation; (6) comment only at submit time (the row is immutable, so a later-added comment is an edit); (7) numeric length limits (no canonical number exists; the live precedents are 2000 chars/8000 octets for messages and report narratives); (8) updating the legal and store declarations that state no free-text review exists; (9) the definition of canonical decision X07.

additions.claim: Block-pair abuse hole specific to free text: the server deliberately lets a blocked or blocking counterpart still review ('A block cannot remove the counterpart's completed-work review entitlement'), the notification is suppressed for blocked pairs, rows are immutable, and a support decision can only have effect NONE. With stars this is a rating; with a public comment it becomes a targeted public message on the blocker's profile that the blocked author can write, the blocker cannot remove, and no operator can hide. Whether the public reader must hide comments authored by a blocked pair (or after a safety report on that Agreement) is an unmade decision, and F143 says a report alone is not an automatic deletion.

additions.claim: Free text can leak private data that the product otherwise gates: after a Dogovor the worker may hold the requester's exact location and phone through access grants (EXACT_LOCATION grants exist on DEV; PHONE channel is used in the readers), and a public comment is the one field where either side can type an address, phone number, email, link or a third party's name. There is no validator, no pattern check and no rate or abuse machinery in the schema, and canonical J23 requires that the private job and address are not part of the review card. Deterministic checks (length in characters and octets as for messages and reports, trimmed, control characters) are possible without AI, but any content rule beyond the existing 2000/8000 precedents would be invented policy and needs an owner decision.

additions.claim: Idempotency hash contract must be frozen for old clients: input_hash is sha256 of jsonb {agreementId,target,rating,tags} (migration lines 77-78) and is the replay key together with client_request_id. A comment-less request from an old or new client must keep exactly that formula (no 'comment': null key), otherwise a lost-ack retry that straddles the rollout returns REQUEST_ID_REUSED and the 7 stored hashes stop matching. When a comment is included, the hash becomes a content-derived fingerprint of free text; the live closure patch already replaces any column named input_hash with the AF-D22 hash (and the CHECK input_hash hex is satisfied by that value), so the column must keep that name or the patch loop will not cover it.
evidence: SQL: prosrc of private.closure_redaction_patch_v5 foreach list contains 'input_hash'

additions.claim: Closure executor mechanics that constrain the patch design: rpc_redact_account_closure_step_service iterates the relations list as steps (totalSteps = cardinality of closure_redaction_relations_v5), selects rows 'where scope and patch is not null for update', records a certificate row per row, applies only the keys of the patch with jsonb_populate_record, then deletes the certificate; closure_redaction_allowed_v5 requires service_role, an EXECUTING closure with adapter OWNER_AF_D22_EVENT_ERASURE_V1, a DISPATCHED RELATIONAL_REDACT action and (after_row-patched keys-updated_at) equal to the before row. A patch such as {comment:null, input_hash:<AF-D22 hash>} is idempotent because the plan function returns null when t@>patch. Closure hard blockers include ACTIVE_AGREEMENT, so a closing account has only COMPLETED or CANCELLED Agreements; exceptions (SCOPED_EVIDENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED, MEDIA_EVIDENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED) are advisory under the adapter.

additions.claim: Cost separation for the owner: the certificate-moving part of D12 is only the storage (column or table, its constraints/trigger/ACL) and the erasure edits. A public paged comment reader is digest-neutral if it is a function outside the 88 plus a plain index: the only index serving target reads is agreement_reviews_target_rating_idx(target_account_id) INCLUDE (rating), which has no created_at ordering, so a keyset-paged reader needs a new index (indexes and policies are not hashed). The reader must also apply closure_account_restricted and safety_pair_blocked checks like rpc_get_account_reputation, and be fenced automatically by rpc_closure_api_guard.
